Plan recovery before each deployment: back up required data and configuration through a separately authorized process, and retain known-good images and their verified digests under your retention policy. A source-promotion rerun is not an image-digest rollback.

  1. Stop the failed run and do not approve later stages. Identify which environments changed from their recorded target, source and image evidence.
  2. Select the last accepted complete pinned combination. Review its compatibility with current configuration, data and application binding using deployment rollback. A source-promotion rerun may rebuild images; it does not guarantee the previous image digest.
  3. For affected environments, restore reviewed stage inputs and rerun the protected flow from the accepted commit with all prerequisite stages selected. Keep WIF identities, scoped permissions and Environment checks in place. Do not approve promotion until Validation passes again.
  4. If abandoning pipeline onboarding, disable the pipeline and have the Azure DevOps administrator revoke only its resource authorizations. Retire newly created WIF connections, grants and variable groups only after confirming no other pipelines use them. Preserve deployed application resources and data.

Rechecking an old commit does not reverse schema, infrastructure or data changes. Use service-specific recovery where required, not environment deletion. Do not relax PNA, bypass auth or weaken promotion conditions to make recovery pass.

This documentation procedure does not establish live pipeline acceptance.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Customize the Agent Application or deploy a different, customer-owned application with pinned deployment inputs. A different application must implement the authentication, UI and ingestion API contracts for any components it reuses.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
Use this runbook when documented configuration is insufficient or you need a different application. Choose the branch that matches your change:

Goal Start here Change a documented setting Deployment settings; no source fork needed Extend the Agent Application orchestrator or tools Agent tools, then pin only changed components below Deploy a different application The custom hosted example and its application definition below

For the Agent Application orchestrator hosted in Foundry, use Foundry IQ for knowledge base retrieval. Custom strategies and tools must implement and test the hosted entrypoint and authorization path before deployment to Foundry. The default remains maf_lite with Foundry IQ.

A source fork or capability profile does not close the protected-retrieval integration gate in the Deploy full stack runbook. Implement and test that identity boundary before using protected documents; do not substitute a strategy flag.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Prepare the platform checkout, Python hook dependencies, Azure sign-in and deployment permissions in the Deploy full stack runbook. Commands below run from the platform root unless stated otherwise.
  • The deployment identity must be able to create scoped role assignments. Private Git sources also require noninteractive read access on the actual runner; Azure sign-in does not authorize Git.
  • Hosted components require the runner's Foundry agent-authoring access on the exact project, plus account read access. Review the hosted deployment permissions for the required scopes.
  • Private deployments require a connected host with private DNS resolution. An ACR build pool does not provide that host's connectivity.
  • For a different application, create a new azd environment through the deployment runbook and select its definition before provisioning.

Definitions and manifests are deployment inputs, not runtime configuration. Keep secrets out of both. For App Configuration updates under label agent-lz and hosted redeployment requirements, follow Deployment settings. Do not restart a Container App to refresh a Foundry-hosted agent.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Choose Customize an Agent Application component for a source change. For a different application, follow Application binding and selection, then Deploy a different application. Inspect the contract reference below when editing the definition.

docs.title: Customize an Agent Application component
docs.text: Prefer configuration first. Fork only runtime repositories whose source you change; an orchestrator extension does not require UI or ingestion forks. Fork or mirror the platform when maintaining deployment inputs or automation. Changing its Git remote does not change component repository URLs.

docs.title: Pin the modified component
docs.text:
For an orchestrator customization:

  1. Implement and test the hosted entrypoint and changed behavior, including Foundry IQ retrieval where relevant. Commit and publish a stable tag.
  2. Update its repo, tag and full 40-character Git commit hash together in the platform manifest.json. The fetch path selects a tag, or branch when no tag is set, then verifies HEAD. A commit hash alone is not a selectable fetch reference.
  3. Set the Agent Application definition's orchestrator source.commit to the same hash. Keep application ID agent-lz-default and unchanged component pins.

  4. Validate:

    python -m config.appdefinition --validate app-definition.json

  5. Commit both pin files together. Follow the Deploy full stack runbook and hosted image preparation, which builds from the manifest-pinned orchestrator. A startup-variable change cannot convert a Container App image into a supported hosted image.

  6. Verify the deployed version and changed behavior through the UI. Test both authorized and denied access to protected content.

Keep manifest names agent-app-ui, agent-app-orchestrator, agent-app-ingestion and definition names ui, orchestrator, ingestion. Hooks use these to map sibling folders. Existing checkouts are verified, not advanced automatically: preserve local work before relocating stale checkouts. Matching HEAD does not detect uncommitted source changes. Run git status --porcelain in each source folder and require no output for the source being built; retain reviewed deployment-input edits separately.

Upstream validation does not cover your modifications. Before deployment, record the previous tested pin files and image provenance for deployment rollback.

docs.title: Private Git authentication
docs.text: Use an approved credential helper, short-lived token or SSH identity with repository read access, including for hosted image preparation. Test it as the deployment runner. Never put credentials in URLs, definitions, environment files or logs. See Azure DevOps for the optional pipeline.

docs.title: Application binding and selection
docs.text:
One azd environment hosts one application ID. Set AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION in that environment with azd env set to select a definition file or containing folder; omission selects the Agent Application. Select it before first provision.

The preup lifecycle hook rejects invalid definitions and changed application IDs before Azure resource creation. The preprovision hook repeats validation for standalone azd provision, but cannot guarantee rejection before azd initializes its resource group. Run azd hooks run preup first for that safeguard. Do not edit a binding to force another application into an existing environment.

Ingestion and additive composition

DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP selects Agent Application composition, not components in an explicit custom definition. Foundation composition remains additive: Agent Application Container App placeholders can remain alongside custom resources. Published ingestion capability describes the platform's ingestion selection; your application must implement uploads if it needs them. If reusing Agent App UI, preserve its upload-gate contract.

docs.title: Deploy a different application
docs.text:
Use samples/custom-app/hosted/. Its minimal Responses server demonstrates deployment and configuration access, not retrieval, conversation storage or the Agent App UI API. Microsoft's Hosted agents documentation describes service protocols and identities; the platform contracts below govern this release's deployment.

  1. Inspect the custom hosted example's app-definition.json, azure.yaml and src/main.py. Keep component/service name agent, the explicit hosted agent name and Responses protocol aligned.
  2. Replace the answer logic, preserving the protocol and health endpoints. Implement authentication, authorization and runtime configuration loading; capability profiles do not implement these behaviors.

  3. Commit source changes. Obtain the full source repository commit:

    git rev-parse HEAD

    Replace the definition's all-zero components[0].source.commit with that value. Run git rev-parse HEAD from the source repository: the shipped src belongs to the platform repository; a separate source repository needs its own HEAD.

    Set the pin in the deployment workspace after checkout; another commit changes HEAD again. Keep source files unchanged. For durable committed inputs in a single-repository layout, consider the prebuilt image digest contract below.

  4. Validate and select in the new environment:

    python -m config.appdefinition --validate samples/custom-app/hosted
azd env set AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION samples/custom-app/hosted/app-definition.json
azd hooks run preup

    Expect validation to pass. This checks schema, folder/service contracts and binding, not image availability or application behavior. Schema validation accepts the all-zero editing marker; deployment requires actual source HEAD.

  5. For a custom-only deployment, set DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY=classic in the azd environment before first provision to suppress the bundled hosted orchestrator selection. This is a custom-definition composition requirement, not a second Agent Application deployment path. The custom hosted component receives its required hosted foundation resources.

    Then provision the selected definition using the Deploy infra only runbook, and run root azd deploy. Its service uses its own source/image contract, not the Agent Application hosted image-preparation handoff.

  6. With the custom hosted example's answer logic, confirm the response names the intended project endpoint. A value of unknown or unavailable indicates missing project configuration or failed configuration access. Check the published outputs and logs, and resolve the issue before proceeding. With your logic, verify actual application behavior and denied-access cases.

The definition id binds the environment; agent names the component/service; sample-hosted-agent names the custom example's Foundry agent. The project endpoint URL is supplied separately at runtime. For a Container App instead, use samples/custom-app/containerapp/ and its matching service file; changing only the hosted example's kind is insufficient.

docs.title: Verify and recover
docs.text:
Retain the definition, service file, source/image pin and environment together. For HEAD mismatches, compare git rev-parse HEAD inside the source folder with the declared pin without disabling validation.

For image-pull or role failures, keep the same application ID and immutable image. Use custom hosted image-pull recovery. Do not substitute another environment's endpoints, broad grants or registry admin credentials. Role propagation can require an explicit retry.

docs.title: Shipped example
docs.text: Inspect the custom hosted example files rather than copying an illustrative payload. Read them at your recorded platform commit; the default branch can advance.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
The authoritative v1 schema defines required fields and allowed values. In particular, names must match services, paths stay inside the application folder, and hosted components cannot set Container App ingress or resources.

Definition settings are validated but not published to App Configuration. Arrange runtime configuration separately.

docs.title: Runtime egress declarations
docs.text:
Each component can declare additional outbound dependencies with egress:

"egress": [
  {
    "fqdn": "api.example.com",
    "protocol": "https",
    "port": 443,
    "purpose": "Retrieve the application's approved reference data"
  }
]

Use exact DNS FQDNs, lowercase http or https, an integer port from 1 to 64000 and a nonblank purpose of at most 256 characters. URLs, paths, wildcards, IP addresses and local hostnames are rejected. Each component supports at most 100 entries; destinations are normalized to lowercase.

An explicit egress: [] means no additional runtime egress and removes that component's ownership of previously generated requirements. Omitting egress remains valid: an enabled legacy component retains its previously owned requirements, but a fresh legacy definition adds none. Removing a component removes its ownership, not another component's shared dependency.

Review the exact source's fixed downloads and configured integrations when editing these declarations. The bundled UI declares []; both orchestrator and ingestion declare the tiktoken asset host over HTTPS/443. A custom definition is additive, so its plan can also include bundled workloads. Follow runtime egress review and reconciliation before provisioning. Build registries and package feeds are configured separately.

docs.title: What a definition cannot contain
docs.text: No lifecycle hooks, Azure role names or remote URLs (except $schema). Configure endpoints separately and grant permissions through capability profiles.

docs.title: Capability profiles
docs.text:
Every component receives base; add only required profiles from the profile catalog. These profiles grant service-resource access to component identities. Configure user consent and document authorization separately, preserving authentication and OBO and Foundry IQ source permissions.

Container App profiles reconcile during post-provisioning. Hosted image pull uses the existing Foundry project managed identity. After deployment verifies the routed agent version and instance identity, it reconciles that instance's declared profiles before greeting smoke. Agent Application orchestrator grants are not substituted; denied or ambiguous assignments fail deployment.

Key Vault targeting and scope resolution follow the role assignment contract; ambiguous resources are not guessed.

docs.title: Folder layout and azure.yaml
docs.text: Keep azure.yaml beside the definition, with a matching service for each component and no project/service hooks. components[].path points to source, not another azd project; align the service's project with it. Hosted services need an explicit agent name and responses or invocations. Deployment reuses the selected environment and deploys each service by name.

docs.title: Source pinning
docs.text:
• source.commit: must equal the local source folder's HEAD. Nothing is cloned; builds include uncommitted working-tree changes.
  • source.imageDigest: requires a qualified service image in azure.yaml. Deployment replaces its tag/digest with the exact declared digest and uses image passthrough, not a new build. All environment substitutions must resolve.

With NETWORK_ISOLATION=true, source Docker builds use ACR_TASK_AGENT_POOL and deploy the resulting digest. Service project must match component path, with Dockerfile and context . there. Unsupported layouts/options fail; provide a prebuilt digest instead. Public builds retain normal azd behavior. See the deployment contract.

Deployment temporarily rewrites image settings in the child azure.yaml and restores it even on failure. Do not edit it or deploy concurrently. Digest pins do not bypass registry authorization. Custom Container Apps using the platform ACR receive registry wiring to their sole attached identity; other registries need separate access configuration. Hosted agents use the project identity's declarative platform-ACR pull grant.

Custom hosted components receive hosted foundation prerequisites even with a Container App layout for the bundled orchestrator; this does not deploy the bundled hosted orchestrator. Reapplying foundation can repair its declared pull grant; refreshing outputs alone cannot. Follow the recovery link above.

docs.title: Reading platform outputs at runtime
docs.text:
Read AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS from APP_CONFIG_ENDPOINT with label agent-lz, as both custom application examples demonstrate. The publisher exposes selected Container App client IDs; hosted instance identities are unavailable during foundation provisioning. See published platform outputs.

The hosted greeting checks for nonempty assistant output using the declared protocol, preferring invocations when both are present. Validate retrieval and authorization with representative tasks and allowed and denied identities.

docs.title: Validate and select a definition
docs.text: Use the validation/selection commands above with your own definition path. Pre-deploy rechecks definition and binding; mismatches exit with code 2. For foundation without application deployment, follow the Deploy infra only runbook.

docs.title: config.appdefinition reference
docs.text: Use python -m config.appdefinition --help for options. The CLI source defines validation, binding checks, environment selection and Container App profile assignment. Do not use binding commands to replace an environment's application.

docs.title: Related pages
docs.text:
• Deploy full stack runbook
  • Hosted agents
  • Deployment settings

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Run definition validation and confirm the environment remains bound to its intended application ID.
  2. In each source folder, compare git rev-parse HEAD with its declared commit. Inspect git status --porcelain; permit only recorded deployment-input edits, not uncommitted application source changes.
  3. Compare the registry digest and selected service/version image with the recorded build or prebuilt digest. Confirm placeholders are no longer serving.
  4. Exercise the changed behavior with allowed and denied identities. For the custom hosted example, confirm configuration access as described in Step 6. Do not accept protected retrieval until its identity integration is proven.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
1. Stop promotion. Restore the previous tested definition and service file, keeping the same application ID. For Agent Application customizations, restore both manifest and definition pins together.
  2. Restore the source checkout to its declared commit, preserving local work separately, or verify the previous immutable image remains available to the runtime identity. Do not replace a digest with a mutable tag.
  3. Preview foundation changes before applying them. Redeploy through the same procedure used above: automatic hosted Agent Application image preparation during deploy, or the custom service's own definition contract.
  4. Restore separately managed settings using recorded values and repeat Validation. Redeployment does not reverse data/schema changes; use an owner-approved recovery plan if the previous application is incompatible.

Do not edit the binding, delete data or broaden permissions to force rollback. Deleting the local definition does not remove Azure resources.

docs.title: Deployment settings
docs.text:
Agent Landing Zone separates:

  • Deployment inputs, supplied through the azd environment or root main.parameters.json. They select resources and the application, and control image builds.
  • Runtime settings, read by applications from Azure App Configuration at startup. Bootstrap values, such as the store endpoint, must be available before remote reads begin.

The default Agent Application uses Foundry hosted orchestration with maf_lite, no panel and native Foundry IQ Blob ingestion. This page explains settings and defaults, not an execution sequence. How it works introduces the concepts; deployment design, capacity and cost planning explain the planning decisions.

The Deploy infra only and Deploy full stack runbooks describe input commands, provisioning and validation. Read individual keys instead of dumping environments that may contain secrets.

Application-specific runtime settings

Runtime settings vary by application. Those described here belong to Agent Application, the supplied reference app; a custom app can have different requirements.

Note

main.parameters.json is the checked-in input to composition. The preprovision hook generates infra/main.parameters.json from it and the selected environment. Do not edit the generated file. In a Git checkout, the hook attempts to hide local regeneration from git status with skip-worktree.

docs.title: Environment boundaries
docs.text:
DEV, TEST and PROD need separate azd environments and resource groups. Separate subscriptions strengthen administrative and quota boundaries. Permissions, identities and dedicated stores enforce the following boundaries.

Boundary Keep separate Target and deployment access Resource group/subscription, azd environment and environment-scoped deployment identity. DEV must not deploy to PROD. Runtime access Component identities, grants and Entra registrations, or explicitly separated callbacks and consent. Configuration and secrets App Configuration store/endpoint and Key Vault. The agent-lz label is shared by convention, not an environment separator. Data Sources, indexes, conversation/history stores and retention. Use approved test data instead of copying production documents. Network and builds DNS, routes, private endpoints and a connected runner. An ACR build pool does not connect the deployment host.

Approved nonsecret inputs can be version-controlled. An environments/ folder is not loaded automatically; its settings need explicit application. Local .azure contains private deployment state, which hooks copy to child projects. Those workspaces need the same protection and cannot safely be copied between DEV, TEST and PROD.

docs.title: Resource naming
docs.text: Resource naming explains defaults, overrides and name stability. Names resolve before the first provision; later changes can create new resources instead of updating existing ones.

docs.title: Resource group destinations
docs.text:
This Agent Bicep/azd interface uses the compatible components pinned by the platform manifest. Terraform and portal do not share this Agent platform contract.

New environments use three resource groups by default: Foundry/grounding, application and workload networking. Existing environments keep their mapping. All workload destinations must be in AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID. Equal names are valid: one, two or three distinct groups can express the same three logical destinations. These inputs do not enable services, change network isolation or create a platform hub; existing BYO VNet, DNS and hub settings still apply.

Variable Default Purpose AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-<environment-name> Foundry and grounding destination, and the native azd root deployment group. An explicitly supplied name is preserved. AZURE_APP_RESOURCE_GROUP <AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP>-app Application destination: Container Apps, registry, App Configuration, Key Vault, application Cosmos DB and monitoring. AZURE_NETWORK_RESOURCE_GROUP <AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP>-network Destination for workload-owned network resources. Existing network/private-endpoint overrides retain their own contract. CREATE_RESOURCE_GROUPS true for new environments Strict boolean (true or false): allows creating missing additional destination groups. Set false to require pre-created additional groups. Does not disable azd's normal root-group creation.

The hook saves these defaults in the selected azd environment before provision. For long custom root names, generated names include a stable hash and suffix within Azure's 90-character limit. These are first-run defaults, not automatic changes to existing environments.

Set destinations before first provision. For three pre-created groups:

azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-ai
azd env set AZURE_APP_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-app
azd env set AZURE_NETWORK_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-net
azd env set CREATE_RESOURCE_GROUPS false

For two groups, set AZURE_NETWORK_RESOURCE_GROUP to rg-ai to keep networking with Foundry, or rg-app to keep it with the application. For one group, explicitly select the same name for all destinations:

azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-workload
azd env set AZURE_APP_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-workload
azd env set AZURE_NETWORK_RESOURCE_GROUP rg-workload

With false, a missing additional destination fails before services are provisioned. With true, existing groups are reused without changing their tags or location; only missing additional groups are created.

The additional destinations are application and network; azd manages creation of the Foundry/root group through its normal lifecycle. New additional groups do not receive the azd-env-name tag.

Run the normal root lifecycle: each azd provision coordinates the resource-group-scoped root and its scoped modules. Do not replace it with three manual deployments. Hosted image preparation still uses its normal multi-step lifecycle.

docs.title: Resource group permissions
docs.text:
• Existing groups: Contributor on each target covers resource management and Microsoft.Resources/deployments/*, not RBAC grants or data access. Splitting existing groups does not itself require subscription Owner or subscription-scope deployment permission.
  • Creating missing groups: CREATE_RESOURCE_GROUPS=true additionally needs Microsoft.Resources/subscriptions/resourceGroups/write at subscription scope. A scoped custom role can grant that action; subscription Contributor is broader, not a universal prerequisite.
  • RBAC: the deploying identity needs Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write at each assignment scope, for example through Role Based Access Control Administrator, subject to its conditions. Creating a group does not automatically grant this access.
  • Service configuration: keep the required Foundry, Search, App Configuration, Key Vault and other service-specific data-plane roles. Management-plane Contributor does not replace them. External network/DNS resources require their owners' scoped permissions.

Resource-group Contributor and scoped RBAC administration do not grant Entra directory reads; for platform-output client-ID discovery, restricted automation can instead supply AGENTLZ_COMPONENT_IDENTITIES as a nonsecret JSON map of Container App component names to pre-resolved managed-identity client IDs, without granting broad directory rights.

The workflow does not elevate its own permissions. It records the mapping with the environment; changing a provisioned environment's mapping is not a supported resource migration. If an existing binding uses a different native root, retain its original implementation or create a new environment rather than retargeting it through environment variables.

After partial failure, repair the cause and retry with the same destinations. Do not delete groups as automatic rollback. Review every destination and shared dependency before any environment removal.

For split-group deployments, a predown safety hook blocks azd down; cleanup requires manual inventory, owner review and separately authorized removal. No automatic deletion or bypass option is provided. The single-group teardown path is unchanged.

docs.title: Values set by azd or by you
docs.text:
A principal is a user or service identity. Its object ID identifies that identity in the Entra directory; it is not an application's client ID.

Variable Description AZURE_ENV_NAME Environment name. Set by azd env new. Used to derive resource names. AZURE_LOCATION Primary Azure region. Set it before provision so the first-run hook can create the additional resource groups. AZURE_PRINCIPAL_ID Object ID of the deployment identity that receives roles for service setup and access. Set by azd from your signed-in account.

docs.title: Inputs that use Bicep defaults
docs.text:
These mappings have no inline default in main.parameters.json. When unset, they use the template defaults shown below.

Variable Template default Description NETWORK_ISOLATION false Set true explicitly for the recommended private production setup. false selects public service endpoints; use it only for approved evaluations without sensitive data. Jumpbox, Bastion and firewall also depend on their component flags. See Network isolation. AZURE_AI_FOUNDRY_LOCATION Deployment region Region for the Microsoft Foundry account. AZURE_COSMOS_LOCATION Deployment region Region for Agent Application Cosmos DB. USE_UAI false Uses user-assigned managed identities instead of system-assigned identities. ENABLE_AGENTIC_RETRIEVAL false Enables the template's agentic retrieval resource configuration. This is separate from the Agent Application setting RETRIEVAL_BACKEND. USE_EXISTING_VNET false Deploys into a virtual network you already have when network isolation is enabled. EXISTING_VNET_RESOURCE_ID Empty Resource ID required when reusing a virtual network. SIDE_BY_SIDE true Selects side-by-side placement for private endpoints and DNS zones rather than placing them in the existing VNet's resource group. See the private endpoint group precedence below.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Variable Default Description AZURE_PRINCIPAL_TYPE User Type of AZURE_PRINCIPAL_ID. Use ServicePrincipal in pipelines. DEPLOYMENT_MODE standalone Declares deployment intent for tags and preflight. ailz-integrated does not automatically attach a hub or override component flags. Supply the hub, routing, resource reuse and DNS inputs explicitly. POLICY_MANAGED_PRIVATE_DNS false Delegates private DNS zone groups/records to Azure Policy. Use instead of BYO private DNS zone IDs; agree policy coverage, VNet links and readiness with the DNS owner. RESOURCE_NAMING_MODE caf Uses Cloud Adoption Framework prefixes and naming tokens. See Resource naming. USE_CAPP_API_KEY false Hosted composition keeps this API-key mechanism disabled. It does not configure Entra ID sign-in. APP_RUNTIME_CONFIGURATION_MODE appConfig The Agent Application reads runtime settings from App Configuration. ENABLE_COSMOS_ANALYTICAL_STORAGE false Enables the Agent Application Cosmos DB analytical store. AZURE_SEARCH_LOCATION Empty Region for both the Agent Application Search service and the separate Foundry Agent Service Search service. Leave empty to use AZURE_LOCATION. AZURE_SPEECH_LOCATION Empty Region for Azure AI Speech. Leave empty to use the deployment region. AZURE_PE_LOCATION Empty Region for private endpoints. Leave empty to use the deployment region. AZURE_PE_RESOURCE_GROUP_NAME Empty Explicit private endpoint group override takes precedence. When empty, USE_EXISTING_VNET=true with SIDE_BY_SIDE=false uses the existing VNet's group; otherwise uses the resolved network group (AZURE_NETWORK_RESOURCE_GROUP). New Foundry-root environments initialize a separate network group; existing single-group environments retain their mapping. EXISTING_APPLICATION_INSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING None Sends telemetry to an Application Insights resource you already have.

Supported EXISTING_* inputs select reuse, subject to each resource's conditions. They are listed in Network and security. Foundry backing-service reuse uses native parameter names instead; see Resource selection and reuse. A supported resource ID selects reuse; naming and deployment flags control resource creation.

docs.title: Agent App Ingestion selection
docs.text:
Variable Fresh-environment default Description DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP false Selects the optional Agent App Ingestion component of the Agent Application, independently of DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY.

The boolean is persisted by pre-provision and published under label agent-lz. Existing environments retain their selection rather than silently adopting the fresh default. Custom definitions retain their declared components and additive infrastructure composition.

Selection Effect false Omits Agent App Ingestion from subsequent Agent Application composition/deployment and reconciliation. The UI disables attachment controls and upload paths, not text chat, authentication or retrieval. true Selects the app and retains the UI's existing upload eligibility checks. It does not grant every caller permission to upload.

Omission supports native Foundry IQ azureBlob, or an explicitly configured, independently populated SEARCH_RAG_INDEX_NAME for ai_search / Foundry IQ searchIndex. It does not select a strategy, configure SharePoint, rewrite source configuration, populate an index or remove authorization. FOUNDRY_IQ_CONVERSATION_UPLOAD_ENABLED=true requires the app.

See Ingestion for native ingestion, conversation uploads and custom processing. Disabling the component does not delete existing resources or revoke their grants.

docs.title: Search region and quota
docs.text:
AZURE_SEARCH_LOCATION resolves the effective Bicep searchServiceLocation. An unset or empty value falls back to AZURE_LOCATION. Both newly created Search services use this effective region. Provider availability and Search quota checks use that same region, not the primary region when an override is set.

Search quota must cover the complete enabled service count: one Agent Application service when deploySearchService (DEPLOY_SEARCH_SERVICE) is enabled, plus one Foundry Search service when deployAiFoundry and deployAAfAgentSvc (DEPLOY_AAF_AGENT_SVC) are enabled and aiSearchResourceId is not supplied.

When both creation paths are enabled, the check requires quota for two services. Reusing a Foundry Search resource does not request a new service for that path. Bypassing preflight does not resolve region mismatches or insufficient quota. See Search preflight region and quota.

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text:
A knowledge source describes retrievable data; a knowledge base combines sources for retrieval. The pattern identifies the setup arrangement, such as native Blob processing or an independently populated Search index. The source kind identifies the data connector. Both default to azureBlob.

Foundry IQ manages the default Blob knowledge source and knowledge base. Native source processing does not require Agent App Ingestion. The application uses the knowledge base for retrieval; source permissions and application authorization still apply.

Variable Default Description RETRIEVAL_BACKEND foundry_iq Retrieval implementation used by the Agent Application orchestrator. FOUNDRY_IQ_PATTERN azureBlob Native Blob source processing and knowledge-base setup. FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_KIND azureBlob Blob connector for the knowledge source. FOUNDRY_IQ_API_VERSION 2026-05-01-preview Azure AI Search API version used for Foundry IQ objects. FOUNDRY_IQ_IS_ADLS_GEN2 false Identifies Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) Gen2: Blob storage with a hierarchical directory namespace. true when the source account uses that namespace. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_NAME knowledge-base Knowledge base name. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONNECTION_NAME knowledge-base-connection Foundry project connection to the knowledge base. FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME knowledge-base-blob-ks Knowledge source name. FOUNDRY_IQ_SEARCH_INDEX_NAME agent-lz-index Search index name.

Other retrieval defaults: billing plan free, semantic configuration default, security field metadata_security_id, storage container documents, content extraction mode standard, ingestion permission options ["rbacScope"], and the filter add-on disabled.

For network-isolated native Blob configuration, infrastructure publishes SEARCH_SHARED_PRIVATE_LINKS as a JSON array under label agent-lz. This is post-provision metadata, not an operator switch or a runtime retrieval setting.

Each entry records the template-owned name, groupId and privateLinkResourceId. Configuration uses these values to verify the Search links and their target Storage and Foundry resources before creating a native knowledge source. Pending links require administrator approval. This deployment-generated metadata is not an operator override. See Private native Blob ingestion.

docs.title: Explicit shared-source permission options
docs.text:
Ingestion permission metadata records access information alongside indexed content. rbacScope records Azure RBAC scopes; sensitivityLabels records information-protection labels. Retrieval must still enforce the applicable permissions for the caller.

FOUNDRY_IQ_INGESTION_PERMISSION_OPTIONS controls the configured source's ingestion permission metadata. Omission or an actual null value retains the protected default ["rbacScope"]. An explicit JSON empty array, [], is an opt-in for a deliberately shared source when native Blob ingestion is active. An empty array is distinct from an omitted setting.

For active native Blob ingestion, the shared-source empty list is accepted with RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=foundry_iq, FOUNDRY_IQ_PATTERN=azureBlob, azureBlob knowledge source kind and a recognized non-ADLS source. Active ADLS Gen2, mismatched source configuration and ambiguous ADLS configuration fail closed. Nonempty Blob permission lists accept only rbacScope and sensitivityLabels.

The infrastructure also publishes [] as unused metadata for inactive native Blob ingestion: ai_search with any pattern, or foundry_iq with the searchIndex pattern. Those empty lists remain accepted because no native Blob knowledge source is rendered. They are not shared-source opt-ins and do not change the independently populated index's authorization.

Malformed JSON, a single value instead of a JSON list, the text null, invalid list entries and unsupported permission names fail with actionable diagnostics. Invalid input fails closed rather than silently removing protection. An actual null and the text null are different inputs.

For active native Blob ingestion, [] is appropriate only when policy permits the source's documents to be shared without that ingestion permission metadata. It does not grant document access by itself or change other sources, application authentication, Entra ID/OBO, retrieval authorization, RBAC or private network restrictions.

It is not a workaround for an authentication or private-link failure. Its use requires audience review and allow/deny tests with real user identities before activation.

Restoring ["rbacScope"] requires source reconfiguration and verification of source/index permission metadata, including already-ingested documents. Allowed and denied users both need validation before access resumes. The Deploy full stack runbook covers reconfiguration. See also Private native Blob ingestion.

docs.title: Network and security
docs.text:
These parameters apply mainly when NETWORK_ISOLATION=true. Network isolation explains connectivity and DNS requirements.

Additional runtime destinations belong in the application's components[].egress, not a blanket network exception or App Configuration key. Review the component plan before provisioning; external firewall policies remain report-only.

Variable Default Description DEPLOY_AZURE_FIREWALL true Deploys Azure Firewall for egress control. ENABLE_FIREWALL_DNS_PROXY false Enables the deployed firewall's DNS proxy only when both Azure Firewall deployment and network isolation are enabled. Does not modify VNet or VPN DNS settings. DEPLOY_ACR_TASK_AGENT_POOL true Deploys an Azure Container Registry agent pool inside the virtual network so images can be built without a local Docker host. The pool is created only when NETWORK_ISOLATION=true. DEPLOY_JUMPBOX Same as NETWORK_ISOLATION Deploys a Windows jumpbox virtual machine. DEPLOY_BASTION Enabled with network isolation and jumpbox deployment Deploys Azure Bastion unless an existing Bastion is selected. BASTION_SKU_NAME Standard Bastion SKU. DEPLOY_NAT_GATEWAY Enabled with network isolation and jumpbox deployment Deploys a NAT gateway unless an existing gateway is selected. ENABLE_ACS_MEDIA_EGRESS false Opens firewall egress for Azure Communication Services media. DEPLOY_GROUNDING_WITH_BING false Deploys Grounding with Bing Search. DEPLOY_KEY_VAULT true Deploys the Agent Application Key Vault. DEPLOY_VM_KEY_VAULT false Deploys a separate Key Vault for the jumpbox. DEPLOY_LOG_ANALYTICS true Deploys a Log Analytics workspace unless an existing workspace is selected. ENABLE_PRIVATE_LOG_ANALYTICS true Configures Azure Monitor Private Link when network isolation is enabled and a central workspace is not being reused. ALLOW_MIXED_OBSERVABILITY_WORKSPACES false Allows Application Insights and Log Analytics from different sources. DEPLOY_SEARCH_SERVICE true Deploys the Agent Application Search service. DEPLOY_SPEECH_SERVICE false Deploys Azure AI Speech (SKU S0). DEPLOY_STORAGE_ACCOUNT true Deploys the document storage account.

Bastion tunneling is disabled by default.

docs.title: Subnet creation and addressing
docs.text:
Choose subnet ownership first. The global DEPLOY_SUBNETS switch and all twelve individual switches default to true through inline environment mappings in root main.parameters.json. Effective creation is networkIsolation && deploySubnets && individualFlag.

Native root parameter Environment input Subnet purpose deploySubnets DEPLOY_SUBNETS Global creation switch for new and existing VNets deployAgentSubnet DEPLOY_AGENT_SUBNET Foundry Agent Service deployAcaEnvironmentSubnet DEPLOY_ACA_ENVIRONMENT_SUBNET Container Apps environment deployPeSubnet DEPLOY_PE_SUBNET Foundry/grounding private endpoints deployAzureBastionSubnet DEPLOY_AZURE_BASTION_SUBNET Bastion deployAzureFirewallSubnet DEPLOY_AZURE_FIREWALL_SUBNET Firewall deployGatewaySubnet DEPLOY_GATEWAY_SUBNET VPN/ExpressRoute reservation deployAppGatewaySubnet DEPLOY_APP_GATEWAY_SUBNET Application Gateway deployJumpboxSubnet DEPLOY_JUMPBOX_SUBNET Jumpbox deployDevopsBuildAgentsSubnet DEPLOY_DEVOPS_BUILD_AGENTS_SUBNET Build agents deployApplicationPeSubnet DEPLOY_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET Application private endpoints deployPowerPlatformSubnet DEPLOY_POWER_PLATFORM_SUBNET Power Platform deployAiGatewaySubnet DEPLOY_AI_GATEWAY_SUBNET AI Gateway

A false creation flag means do not create/manage that subnet; it does not disable its consumer. Every enabled consumer must have an existing, valid subnet in the selected VNet, or be explicitly disabled. No consumer is silently disabled or redirected to another subnet.

For a fresh deployment without Power Platform integration, omit its optional reservation with azd env set DEPLOY_POWER_PLATFORM_SUBNET false. In contrast, disabling application PE subnet creation still requires an existing application PE subnet when application private endpoints are enabled.

An isolated new VNet is still created when subnet creation is disabled, but configuration fails if an enabled workload requires a subnet that is absent. For an existing VNet, only selected subnets are created/updated, through serialized child deployments; its entire subnet collection is not replaced. Managed BYO subnet writes require deployNsgs=true; opting out of a subnet's creation does not remove its existing NSG association. Creation flags are not deletion commands or a guarantee of preserving every previously submitted subnet in a deployment-owned VNet; Azure can reject removal of occupied subnets.

deployAiFoundrySubnet controls the Foundry Agent Service subnet association, not subnet creation. Use deployAgentSubnet for creation ownership.

docs.title: Network selection examples
docs.text:
For a new isolated environment, set azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true, then apply the matching selection.

For a new VNet, keep the default names and address plan unless your network owner requires different ranges:

azd env set USE_EXISTING_VNET false
azd env set DEPLOY_SUBNETS true

For an existing VNet with template-managed subnets, replace the placeholder with its full ARM resource ID and match the subnet inputs to the approved plan:

azd env set USE_EXISTING_VNET true
azd env set EXISTING_VNET_RESOURCE_ID <existing-vnet-resource-id>
azd env set DEPLOY_SUBNETS true

For externally managed subnets, use the same existing-VNet inputs but set azd env set DEPLOY_SUBNETS false. Confirm all required subnets already exist with the configured names, prefixes, delegations and NSG requirements. Then continue with the selected deployment runbook; these inputs do not configure peering, DNS forwarding or runner connectivity.

docs.title: Names and address ranges
docs.text:
All twelve name and prefix parameters can be overridden in root main.parameters.json or through the environment bindings below. Explicit operator values are preserved through composition; the allocation table lists defaults, not mandatory ranges. Reserved service names must retain their required spellings.

Native name parameter Name environment input Native prefix parameter Prefix environment input agentSubnetName AZURE_AGENT_SUBNET_NAME agentSubnetPrefix AZURE_AGENT_SUBNET_PREFIX acaEnvironmentSubnetName AZURE_ACA_ENVIRONMENT_SUBNET_NAME acaEnvironmentSubnetPrefix AZURE_ACA_ENVIRONMENT_SUBNET_PREFIX peSubnetName AZURE_PE_SUBNET_NAME peSubnetPrefix AZURE_PE_SUBNET_PREFIX azureBastionSubnetName AZURE_BASTION_SUBNET_NAME azureBastionSubnetPrefix AZURE_BASTION_SUBNET_PREFIX azureFirewallSubnetName AZURE_FIREWALL_SUBNET_NAME azureFirewallSubnetPrefix AZURE_FIREWALL_SUBNET_PREFIX gatewaySubnetName AZURE_GATEWAY_SUBNET_NAME gatewaySubnetPrefix AZURE_GATEWAY_SUBNET_PREFIX azureAppGatewaySubnetName AZURE_APP_GATEWAY_SUBNET_NAME azureAppGatewaySubnetPrefix AZURE_APP_GATEWAY_SUBNET_PREFIX jumpboxSubnetName AZURE_JUMPBOX_SUBNET_NAME jumpboxSubnetPrefix AZURE_JUMPBOX_SUBNET_PREFIX devopsBuildAgentsSubnetName AZURE_DEVOPS_BUILD_AGENTS_SUBNET_NAME devopsBuildAgentsSubnetPrefix AZURE_DEVOPS_BUILD_AGENTS_SUBNET_PREFIX applicationPeSubnetName AZURE_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET_NAME applicationPeSubnetPrefix AZURE_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET_PREFIX powerPlatformSubnetName AZURE_POWER_PLATFORM_SUBNET_NAME powerPlatformSubnetPrefix AZURE_POWER_PLATFORM_SUBNET_PREFIX aiGatewaySubnetName AZURE_AI_GATEWAY_SUBNET_NAME aiGatewaySubnetPrefix AZURE_AI_GATEWAY_SUBNET_PREFIX

Set vnetAddressPrefixes.value as an explicit array in root main.parameters.json (default ["192.168.0.0/21"]); there is no VNET_ADDRESS_PREFIXES environment mapping. For example, merge this complete address plan into the root file's parameters object before first provision, if 10.20.0.0/21 is approved and does not overlap connected networks:

{
  "vnetAddressPrefixes": {"value": ["10.20.0.0/21"]},
  "agentSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.0.0/24"},
  "acaEnvironmentSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.1.0/24"},
  "peSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.2.0/26"},
  "azureBastionSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.2.64/26"},
  "azureFirewallSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.2.128/26"},
  "gatewaySubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.2.192/26"},
  "azureAppGatewaySubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.3.0/27"},
  "jumpboxSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.3.64/27"},
  "devopsBuildAgentsSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.3.96/27"},
  "applicationPeSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.3.128/26"},
  "powerPlatformSubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.4.0/24"},
  "aiGatewaySubnetPrefix": {"value": "10.20.5.0/24"}
}

A subnet override does not resize the VNet; a reused VNet's actual address space is authoritative. Names must be unique and required names/prefixes cannot be empty. CIDRs must be aligned IPv4 ranges, contained in the VNet and nonoverlapping with other requested or existing subnets. The same managed subnet's current range is not counted twice. Invalid ranges fail rather than being replaced with defaults. Reserved names and service-specific size, delegation and NSG requirements still apply.

docs.title: Application private endpoint subnet
docs.text:
Application private endpoints use their own configured subnet, independently of resource group count.

Variable Native root parameter Default Purpose AZURE_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET_NAME applicationPeSubnetName application-pe-subnet Dedicated application private endpoint subnet name. AZURE_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET_PREFIX applicationPeSubnetPrefix 192.168.3.128/26 Aligned IPv4 CIDR for the application private endpoint subnet.

Enabled application Cosmos DB, Key Vault, App Configuration, Container Apps, ACR and Azure Monitor Private Link Scope private endpoints use the application subnet. Foundry/grounding private endpoints use peSubnetName/peSubnetPrefix, defaulting to pe-subnet at 192.168.2.0/26.

Customize the name and prefix before first provision, using your approved address plan:

azd env set AZURE_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET_NAME snet-app-pe
azd env set AZURE_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET_PREFIX <approved-ipv4-subnet-cidr>

The application subnet needs a distinct name and an aligned IPv4 CIDR of /29 or shorter. Empty required names/prefixes fail explicitly; there is no shared Foundry PE fallback. With DEPLOY_APPLICATION_PE_SUBNET=false or DEPLOY_SUBNETS=false, application endpoints still select this configured subnet. It must already exist and satisfy the enabled consumers' requirements.

docs.title: Hub integration
docs.text:
These parameters describe spoke integration with an existing hub. Hub integration explains the network design.

Variable Default Description HUB_INTEGRATION_HUB_VNET_RESOURCE_ID None Resource ID of the hub virtual network. HUB_INTEGRATION_CREATE_HUB_PEERING true Creates spoke-to-hub peering for a newly created spoke VNet. The hub owner supplies reverse peering. With an existing VNet, both directions are externally managed. HUB_INTEGRATION_PEERING_ALLOW_GATEWAY_TRANSIT false Allows gateway transit on the peering. HUB_INTEGRATION_PEERING_USE_REMOTE_GATEWAYS false Uses the hub gateways from the spoke. HUB_INTEGRATION_EGRESS_NEXT_HOP_IP None Private IP of the hub firewall used as the default route. HUB_INTEGRATION_EXISTING_ROUTE_TABLE_RESOURCE_ID None Route table to attach instead of creating one.

docs.title: Existing resources
docs.text:
Supported resource-ID inputs select reuse instead of creation:

  • EXISTING_VNET_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_JUMPBOX_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_BASTION_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_NAT_GATEWAY_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_RESOURCE_ID
  • EXISTING_APPLICATION_INSIGHTS_RESOURCE_ID

Existing private DNS zones, such as hub-owned zones, use EXISTING_PRIVATE_DNS_ZONE_<ZONE>_RESOURCE_ID, where <ZONE> is one of:

COGSVCS, OPENAI, AISERVICES, SEARCH, COSMOS, BLOB, KEYVAULT, APPCONFIG, CONTAINERAPPS, ACR, AZUREMONITOR, OMSOPSINSIGHTS, ODSOPSINSIGHTS, AZUREAUTOMATION, APPINSIGHTS.

Their owner must provide the required VNet links or resolver forwarding separately from network peering. With POLICY_MANAGED_PRIVATE_DNS=true, Azure Policy manages DNS records instead of the template. Policy coverage and links need agreement with the DNS owner. Policy-managed DNS and explicit existing-zone IDs are mutually exclusive DNS arrangements.

docs.title: Hosted agent
docs.text:
The orchestrator runs as a Foundry hosted agent by default. The hosted-no-panel topology omits the panel and Agent Application Cosmos DB, not Foundry's separate backing services. See Agent hosting for supported capabilities and conversation-history limitations.

Ordinary chat uses history supplied by the UI on each turn. Hosted orchestration does not itself provide durable cross-session history. Continuity, the UI's optional ability to resume a saved conversation, is a separate, gated capability, not enabled by hosted topology alone.

Variable Default Description DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY hosted-no-panel Agent Application topology. See Topologies. DEPLOY_AAF_AGENT_SVC true Enables the Foundry Agent Service capability host. HOSTED_AGENT_NAME agent-app-orchestrator Name of the hosted agent in the Foundry project. HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE agent-app-orchestrator Repository name of the agent image in Container Registry. HOSTED_CONVERSATION_OWNER_BINDING delegated Associates continuity conversations with the authenticated user. Its identity and validation gates are described in Agent hosting. HOSTED_CONTINUITY_ENABLED false Managed activation state for continuity endpoints. Hosted topology alone does not enable them. See Hosted agents. HOSTED_AGENT_SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 60 Idle timeout for server-sent event (SSE) response streams. APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY false Opt-in bootstrap transport for App Configuration and Agent Application Key Vault endpoints. Requires KEY_VAULT_URI and a compatible runtime and hosted definition. Certificate verification remains enabled. See Configuration TLS compatibility.

Hosted provisioning inputs HOSTED_AGENT_CONTAINER_CPU and HOSTED_AGENT_CONTAINER_MEMORY default to 2 and 4Gi. The Agent Application's child hosted-agent/azure.yaml also declares CPU and memory as literal fields; changing those environment variables alone does not resize the deployed agent. Resizing requires a reviewed child-definition change compatible with the provisioned deployment metadata, followed by a new version. See host capacity requirements.

The child definition also fixes the deployed agent name, startup command and protocol versions. Their provisioning inputs alone do not override those deployment fields.

Other hosted defaults: Responses protocol 2.0.0, Invocations protocol 1.0.0, capability key ID v1 and capability TTL 900 seconds. The platform configures continuity history with 100 items and 32000 estimated tokens. These are not character limits or a limit on ordinary session chat. See Hosted agents for the continuity activation and history limitations.

UI continuity configuration explains user-ownership checks, signed access capabilities and conversation storage. These belong to the application runtime, not infrastructure inputs.

PREPARE_HOSTED_AGENT, HOSTED_AGENT_PREPARED and DEPLOY_HOSTED_AGENT are script-managed state, not operator inputs.

APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY is a container environment variable, not an App Configuration key: it is read before remote configuration can load. Only true and false are accepted. The infrastructure's KEY_VAULT_URI output provides the deployed vault URI without hardcoding a cloud DNS suffix and is empty when the vault is not deployed. The manifest-pinned Agent Application and infrastructure combination keeps the loader and hosted definition compatible.

docs.title: Deployment controls
docs.text:
Hook execution and application selection use the variables below. The selected application also affects the resource footprint.

Variable Description BUILD_MODE local uses Docker on the deployment host. acr-task uses Azure Container Registry. Unset values select a mode as described below. RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX false defers post-provision configuration in an isolated deployment. It is not a connectivity bypass. See Post-provision can be deferred. AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING true defers isolated post-provision configuration unless RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX explicitly requests a connectivity check. PREFLIGHT_SKIP true skips regional and infrastructure preflight checks, not application-definition or topology validation. AGENTLZ_REGIONAL_PREFLIGHT_SKIP true skips only the regional quota and availability check. AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION Path to a custom application definition. See Custom applications.

Preflight skip flags are diagnostic controls, not a supported fix for quota, region, permission or network failures.

An explicit BUILD_MODE takes precedence. When it is unset, component scripts first apply recognized USE_DOCKER values: true, 1 or yes select local; false, 0 or no select ACR Tasks. Without either override, network isolation or a configured task pool selects ACR Tasks. Otherwise, usable Docker selects local and unavailable Docker selects ACR Tasks. Explicit local fails if Docker is unusable rather than falling back silently.

Hosted orchestrator image preparation always uses ACR Tasks. BUILD_MODE=local does not change that preparation path or the isolated custom source-build path. See Hosted agents and Custom applications.

docs.title: Runtime settings
docs.text:
Post-provision publishes runtime settings to Azure App Configuration with the label agent-lz. That is the label for platform-owned settings.

The Agent Application components do not read exclusively from agent-lz. Their startup loaders also select other component labels, and later matching selections can overwrite earlier values.

Agent App UI and Agent App Ingestion endpoint loaders end with label_filter=None, which leaves the label filter unset and can read other labels.

The orchestrator uses the explicit null label "\0" for its last selection, which reads unlabelled keys rather than all labels. Unlabelled values can still override agent-lz values.

Conflicting component-labelled or unlabelled values can therefore replace a value written under agent-lz. Environment isolation needs separate stores and identities, not just different labels.

Process variables can also override remote values in the orchestrator and optional ingestion component when allow_environment_variables is enabled. Their parsing differs: the orchestrator recognizes 1, true and yes, whereas ingestion treats any nonempty string, including false, as enabled. This parsing difference is a risk, not a recommended way to override settings.

An unavailable store does not make every component stop: some loaders disable remote reads or use configured fallback paths. Runtime validation therefore needs to confirm the effective settings and authorization behavior, not only that the process started.

Settings are loaded at startup. A changed key requires the affected Container App to restart, or a new hosted version to be deployed, before the new startup configuration is loaded. Running hosted versions are immutable.

Provisioning or post-provision can overwrite deployment-owned keys, so persistent changes need matching deployment inputs. Custom application definitions validate settings but do not publish them; the application must publish its own runtime settings.

The Deploy full stack runbook provides commands, including secret rotation for versioned versus unversioned Key Vault references. Changing deployment selection, RBAC or infrastructure requires the matching full workflow, not just a key edit.

docs.title: Connect Copilot Studio to a private Foundry agent
Objective
docs.text:
Connect a Copilot Studio agent to an existing Microsoft Foundry hosted agent without enabling Foundry public network access.

You will reuse the existing Foundry agent and network, then create a relay flow and a dedicated pilot agent in Copilot Studio.

docs.title: What you'll have after this runbook
docs.text:
A Copilot Studio agent that calls your private Foundry agent through an authenticated Power Automate flow.

The figure shows one regional path, with separate subnets in your Azure VNet.

Foundry receives the flow connection user's identity, not automatically the identity of the person chatting.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
Use this runbook when Copilot Studio needs to call an existing private Foundry agent through an authenticated flow. It is a shared-connection relay, not the native connected-agent setup or automatic per-user delegation.

The delegated subnet is in your Azure VNet, not inside Copilot Studio. It must be dedicated to Power Platform.

It can use the VNet containing the Foundry private endpoint, provided that VNet meets Power Platform's regional requirements. Use different subnets for Power Platform delegation and private endpoints.

Another connected VNet also works if routing, private DNS and HTTPS reach the Foundry private endpoint. Do not reuse the private-endpoint or Container Apps subnet for Power Platform delegation.

Why use a flow in this scenario?

This runbook covers Foundry with Public Network Access (PNA) disabled. It uses a Power Automate flow because the HTTP connector supports virtual network integration, allowing HTTPS requests to reach Foundry through its private endpoint.

The native Microsoft Foundry integration follows a separate setup, outside this procedure.

In the documented lab, native connector requests still arrived through public ingress after VNet association and returned HTTP 403 with PNA disabled; the flow used the delegated private path successfully. These results are specific to that lab, not proof that native integration is impossible in every environment. Evaluate the native integration separately.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Foundry: A running, tested hosted agent. Ask its owner for the stable Responses URL and active agent version. Use the agent endpoint shown in Step 3, not a Container Apps /invocations URL or an Activity endpoint. If using the Agent Application, resolve its protected-retrieval integration gate in the Deploy full stack runbook before using protected sources. A working relay is not evidence of source authorization.
  • Azure network: The platform team has already delivered the Power Platform subnet (default powerplatform-subnet, 192.168.4.0/24, delegated to Microsoft.PowerPlatform/enterprisePolicies), regional connectivity, an enterprise policy and its Azure resource ID, an approved Foundry private endpoint and private DNS. Every subnet referenced by the policy must resolve and reach Foundry over HTTPS. Foundry public network access must be Disabled.
  • Power Platform: A Managed Environment with Dataverse, a maker account allowed to create agents, flows and connections, and a Power Platform administrator to associate the enterprise policy. The administrator needs read access to that Azure policy.
  • Governance: Your data policies permit the trigger and HTTP connector together. Confirm Copilot Studio capacity and premium-connector entitlements; this connector is Premium. Azure hosting and model charges are separate. See agent-flow licensing.
  • Recovery record: Record the current enterprise-policy association and any existing agent-scoped grant. If changing an existing solution, export/version it before editing and retain its connection-reference settings. Use a dedicated pilot agent so disabling the relay does not interrupt unrelated topics.

Creating Azure network resources is outside this procedure. The enterprise policy must reference the required regional networks and be associated with the environment. Use the Power Platform setup requirements if the platform handoff is incomplete.

Use the required regional VNets for the Power Platform environment. Geographies with multiple supported regions require two VNets in the specified Azure regions; every delegated subnet must reach Foundry privately. The figure illustrates one regional path, not the complete regional setup.

Foundry uses the connection user's permissions

This procedure uses a specific, shared connection signed in as an approved Microsoft Entra user in the Foundry tenant. Foundry sees that connection user, not automatically the person chatting in Studio. Do not use it for user-specific document permissions unless your application independently enforces them. Require authentication, restrict the Studio agent to approved users and approve the data they can all access.

Per-user connections require a separate identity and channel design; they are not enabled by forwarding a user name in the prompt. See flow connection credentials.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Complete Steps 1-4 in order with the named administrators and maker, then run Validation before publishing to users.

docs.title: Step 1: Associate the environment with the private network
docs.text:
A Power Platform administrator performs this step. Schedule the change: it affects other supported workloads in the environment and can cause up to 30 minutes of connection instability.

  1. In the Power Platform admin center, open Manage > Environments, select the target environment and record its Environment ID from Details. Select this same environment in Copilot Studio and Power Automate.
  2. Open Security > Data and privacy > Azure Virtual Network policies. Select the environment, select the prepared policy and Save. If the association is already correct, make no change.
  3. Open Manage > Environments, select the environment, then History. Wait for the policy operation to show Succeeded before testing.
  4. Have the platform team confirm private DNS, routing and HTTPS access from each delegated regional subnet, not just from the jumpbox.
  5. In the Azure portal, open the Foundry resource's Networking settings. Confirm public network access is Disabled and the intended private endpoint connection is Approved. Do not change either setting to get a successful test.

Expected result: The Managed Environment is linked to the intended policy, and all its regional paths can reach the Foundry private endpoint.

docs.title: Step 2: Authorize the connection user
docs.text:
Have an authorized Azure RBAC administrator grant the connection user Foundry Agent Consumer on the specific agent, if equivalent access is not already present. This allows invocation without authoring access. The agent's own identity and downstream permissions are separate; do not replace them with the connection user's identity.

PowerShell: grant access to this agent only

Run with PowerShell 7 and Azure CLI. Replace every placeholder; use the object ID of the user who will sign in to the connection, not an app client ID. Copy Object ID from that user's Overview in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

$subscriptionId = "<subscription-id>"
$agentScope = "/subscriptions/$subscriptionId/resourceGroups/<resource-group>/providers/Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/<foundry-resource>/projects/<project>/agents/<agent>"
$connectionUserObjectId = "<connection-user-object-id>"

az login
az account set --subscription $subscriptionId
az role assignment create `
    --assignee-object-id $connectionUserObjectId `
    --assignee-principal-type User `
    --role "eed3b665-ab3a-47b6-8f48-c9382fb1dad6" `
    --scope $agentScope `
    --query "{id:id,scope:scope}" --output json

Expected result: The assignment targets the intended user and agent. Keep the returned id for rollback if this is a new pilot-only grant, and allow time for the permissions to take effect. Do not grant subscription Owner, broad Contributor or extra project-authoring roles to resolve an invocation failure. See Foundry RBAC and agent scopes.

docs.title: Step 3: Create the authenticated agent flow
docs.text:
In Copilot Studio, select Flows > New flow > Agent flow. Use the environment from Step 1 and name the flow Call private Foundry agent. Keep it in a solution so it can be moved with its connection reference; the solution is the deployment package for these items.

Use the flow's expression editor

In this step, paste expressions into the flow designer's Expression editor (fx), not as plain text. Step 4 uses Copilot Studio's Formula tab instead.

docs.title: Input and connection
docs.text:
1. In When an agent calls the flow, add one Text input named message. Open the trigger's Code view / Peek code and find the property whose title is message. Its generated key is text in the tested designer; message is only the display name. Use the actual key in the body expression.
  2. Between the trigger and Respond to the agent, add Invoke an HTTP request from HTTP with Microsoft Entra ID (preauthorized). Do not use Get web resource; it is not supported with VNet delegation.
  3. Create a connection with Log in with Microsoft Entra ID, using:
Connection field Value Microsoft Entra ID Resource URI (Application ID URI) https://ai.azure.com Base Resource URL https://<foundry-resource>.services.ai.azure.com Sign-in account The connection user authorized in Step 2

"Preauthorized" refers to the Microsoft application used by the connector. Requests use HTTPS and the connection user's Microsoft Entra identity. The agent-scoped permissions from Step 2 authorize access to Foundry.

Do not append the project path to the base URL or use the resource hostname as the token audience. Do not supply a bearer token, API key or client secret. If tenant policy blocks the connector or requires consent, stop and have the administrator review the connector's permission requirements; do not bypass the policy with another connector.

docs.title: HTTPS request
docs.text:
Keep the action name Invoke an HTTP request. The expressions below reference its internal name, Invoke_an_HTTP_request; check that name in Code view if the designer adds a suffix. If it differs, update every body(...) reference in the response expression below.

Request field Value Method POST URL The fixed agent Responses URL below Header Content-Type: application/json Retry policy None for the pilot; a repeated POST can duplicate work 
https://<foundry-resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>/agents/<agent>/endpoint/protocols/openai/responses?api-version=v1

Use the exact stable Responses URL from the agent's Publish dropdown in Foundry, or ask its owner for it. Do not substitute display names into the template. Do not let the chat user or generative orchestration choose the URL, method, headers or connection.

API version is not the agent version

Keep api-version=v1 unchanged. Foundry selects the active agent version behind the stable URL; do not add that version to the URL. Record and verify it before acceptance.

For Body, select Expression and paste this expression, without @{...}:

string(setProperty(json('{"store":true,"stream":false}'), 'input', triggerBody()?['text']))

Replace text only if the trigger uses another property. Constructing the object before serializing it preserves quotes, line breaks, backslashes and Unicode. Do not concatenate the user's message into a JSON string.

The flow waits for a complete response; it does not stream tokens. store:true requests response storage; approve Foundry's retention settings before using real data. Each call sends only the current message, so the relay has no multi-turn history.

docs.title: Response and publication
docs.text:
In Respond to the agent, add a Text output named foundry_response. Set its value using Expression:

if(contains(body('Invoke_an_HTTP_request'), '$content'), base64ToString(body('Invoke_an_HTTP_request')?['$content']), string(body('Invoke_an_HTTP_request')))

This decodes the response to JSON text, whether the connector returns JSON directly or inside a base64 $content envelope. Step 4 extracts the chat reply from this JSON.

Select Respond to the agent > Settings and configure:

  • Run After: Run only when Invoke an HTTP request is successful. Do not select failed, skipped or timed-out states.
  • Networking: Set Asynchronous response = Off.

Save and Publish the flow. In Power Automate, open its details page, then Run only users > Edit. For the HTTP connector, select the specific authorized connection, not Provided by run-only user, and save the settings.

In Solutions, open your team's solution and confirm the flow is listed. If not, select Add existing > Automation > Cloud flow, select the flow and Add. If needed, create a solution first.

Expected result: The published flow has one text input, one authenticated POST and one text output. Its complete synchronous execution must stay within the 100-second agent-action limit. Streaming and background completion are not handled by this relay.

docs.title: Step 4: Relay the actual response in Copilot Studio
docs.text:
In Copilot Studio, create or open a dedicated pilot agent. The topic below handles every nonempty message; do not add it unchanged to an agent with other routing responsibilities. Require user authentication and restrict sharing before adding real users.

  1. Open Topics > Add a topic > From blank and name it Private Foundry relay. On the Trigger node, select Change trigger > A message is received, then Edit. In the trigger's Condition, switch Builder > Formula and enter !IsBlank(System.Activity.Text). This is a trigger property, not a separate Condition node.
  2. Add Add a tool, select the published Call private Foundry agent flow, and bind its message input to the system variable System.Activity.Text (the user's current message). For foundry_response, create a Text topic variable named FoundryResponse, shown as Topic.FoundryResponse.

  3. Add Variable management > Set a variable value. Under Set variable, select Create new and name the variable FoundryReply (shown as Topic.FoundryReply). For To value, select Formula and paste the expression below; the resulting variable must be Text. Tool calls can precede message items in the response. The expression reads every output_text part in those messages.

    Power Fx: extract text only from a completed, error-free response 

    IfError(
    With(
        { r: ParseJSON(Topic.FoundryResponse) },
        If(
            Text(r.status) = "completed" && IsBlank(r.error),
            Concat(
                Filter(Table(r.output), Text(Value.type) = "message") As m,
                Concat(
                    Filter(Table(m.Value.content), Text(Value.type) = "output_text") As c,
                    Text(c.Value.text),
                    Char(10)
                ),
                Char(10)
            ),
            Blank()
        )
    ),
    Blank()
)

  4. Add a Condition node. In its ... menu, select Change to formula, open the formula editor and enter IsBlank(Topic.FoundryReply) || IsMatch(Topic.FoundryReply, "\s*", MatchOptions.Complete).

    In the true branch (missing or whitespace-only text), send: "The Foundry agent did not return a completed text response. Please contact the support team." Do not display raw JSON or retry the POST automatically.

    In All Other Conditions (false), add Send a message and insert the Topic.FoundryReply variable, without a generative rewrite. Insert its value with the variable picker; do not type its name as message text.

  5. End both branches with Topic management > End all topics. Do not enable a second Foundry tool as an automatic fallback. Run the topic checker, fix every error, then save.

    6. Expected result: One message invokes the flow once and displays Foundry's actual text. Invalid JSON, an incomplete/failed response or missing text produces an explicit failure message. If the HTTP action itself fails, Studio's error handling must report the failed action, not substitute a generated answer.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Use harmless test data in a new Studio test conversation and record the UTC test window. In Power Automate, open the flow's details page and select the matching run in Run history. Keep its run ID; expand the HTTP action to inspect its status and outputs, and Respond to the agent for the decoded JSON. Correlate this run with the Studio topic trace to verify backend execution.

Check Acceptance evidence Request integrity A message containing "quotes", a newline, C:\test\file and café reaches the flow unchanged. Use an echo-capable test agent if exact round-trip comparison is needed. Real Foundry execution The matching flow run shows HTTP 200, decoded status: completed, no non-null error, and real output_text. Check the selected agent/version in available response or runtime diagnostics. Private ingress Foundry public network access is still Disabled. Have the platform team correlate the UTC test window and target resource with existing Foundry gateway diagnostics or equivalent approved network evidence; the source must be the delegated private path, not a public connector address. No hidden fallback The topic trace invokes the intended flow once and sends its returned text. A failed action or invalid response gives an error, not a plausible generated reply. Authorization An approved pilot user can invoke the Studio agent; a user outside the shared audience cannot. Separately confirm that the connection identity and agent cannot expose data outside the approved shared-data boundary. Runtime limit Representative calls complete below 100 seconds, including connector and agent processing.

Use existing approved diagnostic settings; do not turn on prompt or document capture just to obtain network evidence. Verify the delegated subnet path separately from jumpbox connectivity. If gateway logs are unavailable, record private ingress as awaiting independent verification.

After these checks pass, return to the Studio agent and select Publish. Repeat the test from the intended authenticated channel with an approved pilot user to validate channel authentication, sharing and connection behavior.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check and action Public access is disabled / HTTP 403 Confirm the flow ran in the associated environment, uses Invoke an HTTP request from the exact connector, and the policy operation succeeded. Inspect the ingress source before changing RBAC. Do not enable Foundry public network access. DNS failure or timeout Have the platform team check DNS, peering/routes, NSGs and HTTPS from every delegated regional subnet. Each path referenced by the policy must reach the private endpoint. HTTP 401 / authorization 403 Verify the connection user's tenant, https://ai.azure.com audience, connection health and agent-scoped invocation access. Distinguish connector-consent errors from Foundry RBAC errors; allow role propagation. HTTP 404 / unsupported endpoint Compare the fixed URL, project and agent with the tested stable Responses endpoint. Do not substitute Activity, Container Apps or another API version. Response contains $content, or Studio shows base64 Apply the Step 3 decoder and check the HTTP action's internal name. Failed/empty response despite HTTP 200 Inspect the decoded response status, error and output types in restricted run history. The agent must return a completed text response; the relay does not render files or handle tool approvals. Flow is missing from the tool picker Check the selected environment, solution membership, published state and required trigger/response actions. Topic checker rejects the formula Confirm Topic.FoundryResponse is Text, paste into the Formula tab, and preserve the As m / As c aliases. Use commas as Power Fx argument separators. Studio action times out Check full execution time and synchronous response settings. Optimize the agent or design an explicit asynchronous integration; do not increase retries or send a fake success.

Restrict run-history access. After validation, apply your organization's Secure inputs / Secure outputs policy to HTTP and response actions: these can contain prompts, retrieved data and replies. Share only sanitized UTC timestamps, run/request IDs and status codes.

docs.title: Operate or stop the integration
docs.text:
• Change: Export/version the solution and record the endpoint, active agent version and connection reference before editing. Rebind the connection in each target environment and repeat Validation after an agent, policy or identity change.
  • Maintain: Assign an owner for connection reauthentication, monitor failures, latency and capacity, and review access and response-retention policies. This relay supplies neither multi-turn history nor the chat user's identity in Foundry.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
1. Disable the relay topic and republish the dedicated Studio agent, then turn off the Call private Foundry agent flow in Power Automate. Test from the published channel and confirm the relay no longer reaches Foundry.
  2. For an update to an existing relay, restore the previous versioned solution through the approved solution-import process, rebind its intended connection reference and repeat Validation before re-enabling it. Importing a solution does not restore Foundry data or the active agent version.
