  3. If Step 2 created a pilot-only RBAC assignment, have its administrator remove that exact recorded assignment ID after confirming it is not shared. In Azure Access control (IAM) at the recorded agent scope, verify the principal and role before removing it. Preserve pre-existing grants.
  4. Keep the delegated subnet, private endpoint and environment VNet policy. If Step 1 changed an existing association, the Power Platform administrator must review its other consumers before restoring the recorded association through the same policy screen. Verify those workloads after any restoration.

Do not detach shared networking or delete connections used by other flows as routine rollback. Keep Foundry PNA disabled and retain authentication throughout.

docs.title: Cost planning
docs.text:
Cost depends on the Agent Landing Zone configuration that runs: topology and resource reuse, capacity and usage. The default has a Foundry hosted orchestrator, frontend, no panel and native Foundry IQ Blob ingestion, without Agent App Ingestion.

This page explains cost drivers, not deployment steps. The Deploy infra only and Deploy full stack runbooks cover execution.

Pricing sources and dates

This page does not quote or reprice Azure services. The shared resource inventory and estimates uses May 29, 2026, East US 2, US dollars, pay-as-you-go example prices. Its scenarios are not Agent Application defaults or a full-stack quote. The shared cost guide explains its calculator example's date and limitations. An estimate needs current regional rates, currency and your organization's agreement.

docs.title: Estimate inputs
docs.text:
Input What it contributes Resolved resources Platform Git commit or release tag, selected application, DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY, ingestion selection, network mode and reused resources. Composed parameters and the deployment preview show planned resources; the deployed inventory also reveals retained allocations. Allocated capacity Search services, registry tier, App Configuration, workload-profile nodes, private endpoints, firewall, Bastion and ingress can incur idle-period charges. Measured usage Turns, model/tool calls, tokens, embeddings, indexing, compute, requests, data, logs and transfer. Initial corpus ingestion and reindexing are separate from steady-state traffic. Shared services Hub, DNS, gateway and monitoring costs allocated with their owners. Reuse avoids some new allocations, not all usage charges.

The Azure Pricing Calculator supports a dated estimate with explicit assumptions and exclusions. Actual spend after deployment provides the comparison baseline.

docs.title: Agent-specific cost drivers
docs.text:
Decision Include in the estimate Application hosting Foundry hosted compute, plus the frontend and other selected components separately. The root's main D4 profile has a zero-node minimum, but selected Container Apps with minimum replicas can keep a node allocated and billed while idle. Foundry Agent Service Separate Search, Storage and Cosmos DB backing resources where created. hosted-no-panel omits Agent Application Cosmos DB, not these Foundry backing resources. Reused dedicated backing resources still have costs. Retrieval and ingestion Agent Application Search replicas/partitions plus any separately billed retrieval features, model calls and embeddings. Omitting Agent App Ingestion does not remove native ingestion or indexing charges. With the component selected, include its compute and processing dependencies. Private networking Count the actual private endpoints, DNS, firewall/NAT, peering/data transfer and connected runner. Include Bastion, VM and disks only where selected or retained. Hub reuse changes allocation and ownership, not the connectivity requirements. Builds and images Registry capacity/storage, ACR Tasks or private agent-pool allocation and build activity. Check the pool's provisioned allocation, not only elapsed build duration. Include image retention and promotion copies. UI ingress or AI Gateway Add Application Gateway/WAF only if enabled. A separately operated AI Gateway has its own tier, capacity, policy and usage charges; it is not included automatically in an Agent deployment. Observability and protection Workspace ingestion/retention, configured tests, backup and redundancy. Avoid double-counting Application Insights ingestion billed through its Log Analytics workspace.

Model deployment sku.capacity allocates quota. To estimate model charges, use the deployment type, region, expected tokens and any provisioned-capacity commitment with the current service prices.

docs.title: Spend controls and security
docs.text:
Azure Cost Management budgets and alerts notify; they do not automatically stop resources or cap spend. Service-level usage after ingestion and representative traffic can reveal idle allocations, retained resources, retry loops and excessive logs.

Model choice, Search capacity, replica minimums and retention can be tuned against measured quality, latency, availability and compliance needs. Each change affects sizing as well as cost.

Shared infrastructure needs approved ownership, routing and permissions. Public access, removed authorization and bypassed private-link readiness are not cost controls. Selection flags affect future deployments; existing resources and grants require separate dependency, backup and access review before cleanup, as covered by the Deploy full stack runbook.

An environment estimate records its owner, date, region/currency, selected/reused resources, expected monthly usage and contingency. Topology, model, corpus or traffic changes can invalidate it. The shared cost guide provides additional pricing references without repeating the generic catalog here.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Deploy the Azure infrastructure and the Agent Application with its default layout: Foundry hosts the orchestrator, Agent App UI runs in Container Apps, and Foundry IQ manages source ingestion and retrieval. The default hosted-no-panel layout omits the administrative panel and Agent Application Cosmos DB. Foundry can require separate backing resources.

docs.title: What you'll have after this runbook
docs.text:
Your Agent Application deployed with a Container Apps UI, a Foundry-hosted orchestrator and native Foundry IQ ingestion and retrieval.

Deployment options

This diagram illustrates the default hosted application layout, not a fixed list of resources for every deployment.

Optional components are included only when enabled. The actual resources depend on your application, network and deployment settings; existing resources may be reused.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text: Use this runbook for a new Agent Application deployment or to add it to its already configured Agent foundation. For a customer-owned application, use the Bring your own app runbook. Only need infrastructure? Use the Deploy infra only runbook. For the relationship between the template, its manifest and lifecycle hooks, see How it works.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Permissions: Contributor for resource deployment plus Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write at the required scopes, for example through Role Based Access Control Administrator. Service configuration needs separate data-plane roles. Shared networks, DNS and monitoring can require additional scoped access. Subscription Owner is not a blanket prerequisite; see resource group permissions and foundation permissions.
  • Subscription readiness: accepted Responsible AI terms, registered resource providers, supported service/model regions and sufficient quota for the selected parameters. Review regional considerations for constraints that preflight cannot eliminate.
  • Private deployments: an authorized deployment host connected to the Azure virtual network (VNet), directly or through a virtual private network (VPN). It must resolve private service hostnames. An Azure Container Registry (ACR) Tasks build pool is not that host.
  • Identity inputs: obtain the delegated Foundry audience and tenant consent plan from your identity administrator. HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE must be that audience followed by /.default, for example https://ai.azure.com/.default when that is the deployed audience. It is not the UI's api://<client-id>/user_impersonation login scope.
  • Application access: arrange the Entra registration, HTTPS callback, Key Vault credential reference and user permissions in Application authentication. Deployment does not perform tenant consent.

Protected retrieval is an integration gate

The shipped hosted entrypoint does not receive the browser's bearer token. The default maf_lite strategy uses a direct Foundry IQ connector, but does not implement the complete authenticated Foundry Toolbox path for per-user protected retrieval. UI on-behalf-of (OBO) sign-in authenticates the Foundry call; it does not close that downstream integration gap.

Assign a developer to implement and validate the supported identity path before admitting protected data. No topology, strategy or permission flag makes this turnkey. Do not enable anonymous retrieval, use service identity or weaken source permissions to make a test pass.

Tool Required for Azure Developer CLI (azd) and Azure CLI (az) Provisioning and lifecycle hooks; use current supported versions PowerShell 7 Windows hooks and cross-platform preflight checks Bash, jq and curl on Linux/macOS POSIX hooks and dependency bootstrap Git Fetching selected, pinned application sources Python 3.12 with pip and venv Validation, composition and service configuration Foundry agents azd extension (azure.ai.agents) Hosted deployment; install with azd extension install azure.ai.agents if absent

Blocks marked bash use Bash syntax. In PowerShell, put commands with a trailing backslash (\) on one line and remove the continuation backslashes. Replace every <placeholder>. Run powershell blocks as written.

Cost and time

Provisioning creates billable resources before the application is ready. Review the foundation inventory and cost scenarios and cost guide, then budget for application runtime, model usage and data. First deployments take longer because of resource creation, image builds, role propagation and private-link approvals. No fixed completion time is guaranteed.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text: Run Steps 1-4 in order. After selecting a checkout, run lifecycle commands from its platform root with the intended environment selected.

docs.title: Step 1: Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Azure/agent-landing-zone.git
cd agent-landing-zone

The checkout's manifest.json pins the compatible runtime components; the deployment hooks fetch them automatically.

Alternatively, azd init -t Azure/agent-landing-zone initializes the current default template in an empty directory. Reuse the environment it creates rather than creating it again in Step 2.

docs.title: Prepare Python
docs.text:
From the repository root:

python -m venv .venv

On Linux/macOS, use python3 if python is unavailable. Activate .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell or source .venv/bin/activate in Bash. Install the dependencies:

python -m pip install -r config/requirements.txt

Keep this environment active for the lifecycle commands.

docs.title: Working from your own repository
docs.text:
An unmodified deployment needs only the platform checkout. Hooks fetch selected runtime components automatically; four forks are not required. Fork or mirror the platform when you maintain deployment inputs or automation, and fork only the runtime components whose source you change.

Keep reviewed, nonsecret inputs in source control and apply them explicitly with azd env set; an environments/ folder is not loaded automatically. Protect .azure/, credentials, sibling component workspaces and deployment logs. For private components, configure Git read access on the actual deployment host separately from Azure authentication. Never embed tokens in repository URLs. See Custom applications for source pinning and composition.

docs.title: Step 2: Select the deployment target
docs.text:
The following creates a new environment. Replace all placeholders:

az login
azd auth login
az account set --subscription <subscription-id>
azd env new <environment-name>
azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <subscription-id>
azd env set AZURE_LOCATION <region>

For an existing environment, use azd env select <environment-name> instead and preserve its approved inputs. Isolate DEV, TEST and PROD with separate environments, resource groups, identities, configuration stores, secrets and data. Promote the same reviewed source revision with stage-specific inputs.

New environments use three resource groups: rg-<environment-name> for Foundry, rg-<environment-name>-app for the application and rg-<environment-name>-network for workload networking. To choose a different Foundry/root name, set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP before provision. The hook creates missing additional groups by default; the deploying identity needs permission to create them. To reuse pre-created groups or select one or two groups, set the resource group destinations now. Existing environments keep their mapping.

docs.title: Step 3: Choose the application and network
docs.text: Set the deployment choices below in the selected azd environment with azd env set before provisioning. Settings containing lists or groups of related fields go in the root main.parameters.json file, as described in the linked infrastructure choices. How it works explains input processing; Deployment settings identifies input ownership.

docs.title: Orchestrator topology
docs.text:
Set the default layout explicitly for this new environment. DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY chooses the runtime layout, not the VNet design:

azd env set DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY hosted-no-panel
azd env set HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE <approved-foundry-audience>/.default
azd env set DEPLOY_INGESTION_CONTAINER_APP false

Expect no administrative panel or Agent Application Cosmos DB. Preserve the recorded layout when recovering an existing environment. See Hosted agents for separately configured capabilities. Keep the runtime strategy AGENT_STRATEGY=maf_lite and retrieval backend RETRIEVAL_BACKEND=foundry_iq; inspect their effective agent-lz settings after service configuration. Runtime keys are not all azd env inputs.

docs.title: Ingestion and custom applications
docs.text:
Use native Foundry IQ ingestion for the configured Blob source. Keep its protected source policy; source ingestion does not prove user-authorized retrieval works. Review Ingestion if conversation uploads or custom processing are required. They are additional capabilities, not default deployment steps.

For a different application, stop here and follow the Bring your own app runbook before first provision. One environment binds to one application ID.

docs.title: Network and build mode
docs.text:
Use private networking for production and workloads with sensitive data. Choose a self-contained private network or a private connection to your organization's existing hub.

The template defaults to NETWORK_ISOLATION=false, so set true explicitly before provisioning a private environment. Public endpoints are an exception for approved, short-lived evaluations or demonstrations without sensitive data, not the recommended production setup.

Choice Inputs and preparation Private, self-contained network azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true; review the standalone design Private spoke using an existing hub NETWORK_ISOLATION=true, explicit hub routing, peering, DNS and shared-service inputs from the hub-and-spoke reference Existing VNet Choose subnet ownership and apply the matching inputs; review delegations and NSGs before provision Public service endpoints, evaluation only Read the public-endpoint conditions and commands first. Authentication does not make an endpoint private.

Apply the approved foundation inputs from infrastructure choices. Do not change NETWORK_ISOLATION on an existing environment as a retry shortcut. With isolation enabled, run configuration, preparation and deployment from the connected host. If creating that host first, use the deferred post-provision procedure.

Image build path Selection Public registry, remote builds Set BUILD_MODE to acr-task with the command below; builds use regular ACR Tasks Private registry, remote builds Also set DEPLOY_ACR_TASK_AGENT_POOL to true before provision; builds use the provisioned VNet pool 
azd env set BUILD_MODE acr-task

For the private registry path, also run:

azd env set DEPLOY_ACR_TASK_AGENT_POOL true

Hosted image preparation uses Azure Container Registry (ACR) Tasks, not local Docker. With isolation enabled, keep the private build pool. See network isolation for build egress, DNS and private-link readiness requirements.

docs.title: Step 4: Deploy
docs.text: Deployment has two stages: provision creates and configures the Azure resources; deploy builds and publishes the application. Run both from the platform root with the same azd environment selected.

docs.title: Before you deploy
docs.text:
Confirm the runner has Foundry agent authoring access on the exact project (Foundry User or an appropriate equivalent), account read access and the required scoped role-assignment authority. Review private-runner permissions and hosted identities for the required scopes.

Review the resource scopes, public access, routes and role changes before approving provisioning. Also review the application's outbound network requirements with python -m config.deployment.egress --plan --environment <environment-name>. Deployment applies managed firewall rules automatically. If you use an external firewall, give the generated report to its owner to arrange the required access.

docs.title: Default Foundry orchestrator (hosted-no-panel)
docs.text:
For a new environment, run these commands in order:

azd provision
azd deploy

Alternatively, run azd up to perform both stages in one command. These commands work on Windows, Linux and macOS. The normal deployment runs its configuration checks automatically; no manual preparation command is needed.

Optional: check configuration before provisioning

For an early check before azd provision, the following commands show the selected subscription, environment and region, then validate the application definition and check that it matches the environment:

azd env get-value AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
azd env get-value AZURE_ENV_NAME
azd env get-value AZURE_LOCATION
azd hooks run preup

Running this check manually is recommended but optional. azd provision also validates the configuration; azd up runs preup automatically.

Stage Result Provision Creates the foundation and configures its services; no running hosted agent or placeholder image is created Deploy: image Automatically fetches the pinned orchestrator source, builds its hosted image when needed, records an immutable digest and binds it to the existing foundation Deploy: applications Creates the hosted version, bootstraps its limited runtime grants, tests a greeting and deploys selected apps

Image preparation is part of azd deploy; no separate preparation command or second provision is required. If provisioning deferred configuration, complete that work from a connected host before deployment. Do not replace the digest with an image tag or bypass permission, network or configuration failures.

For an already configured infrastructure-only environment, reuse the same checkout, inputs and bound application, then run azd deploy. Review hook logs even after success: some configuration sections can log failures and continue. Resolve those failures before validation.

Optional: preview infrastructure changes before deployment

You do not need a preview for the normal deployment above. If you want to run azd provision --preview, first follow the preview preparation instructions. Unlike normal provisioning, preview skips the preparation hook, so you must prepare the selected environment's parameters and any additional resource groups first. This preparation can create resource groups. Neither preparation nor preview confirms that private application connections work.

For an initial deployment, continue to Validation now. Use the maintenance procedures below only for a later operational change.

docs.title: Lifecycle preparation
docs.text: Run these tasks from the platform root with the intended environment selected, Python active, both CLIs authenticated and private connectivity available when required. Record the source revision, manifest, definition, approved inputs and hosted digest before a change. Back up configuration and relevant data using service-specific procedures.

docs.title: Reapply a reviewed deployment
docs.text:
1. Select the reviewed compatible source and pin files. Keep the platform's infra/ with that source, rather than replacing only that directory.
  2. Preserve the environment's layout, component selection, names and source bindings. Back up affected data and separately managed configuration.
  3. If previewing, follow the selected-environment preparation, then review infrastructure changes with azd provision --preview.
  4. Run Step 4. Deployment prepares the image automatically, including when its recorded generated-source provenance is stale.
  5. Repeat Validation before promotion.

docs.title: Redeploy applications only
docs.text:
When foundation outputs, application binding and component selection remain compatible:

azd deploy

Agent Application Container Apps use the manifest's verified sibling checkouts. Preserve local work and relocate a stale checkout so the hook can fetch the selected revision; it does not advance an existing checkout automatically. Child logs are under each component's .logs directory and can contain sensitive details.

Hosted deployment reuses a generated digest only when its recorded source pin and startup command match. Missing or stale generated images are built during azd deploy, without another provision. An operator-managed digest is not rebuilt automatically: verify its provenance, compatibility and registry availability. When rebuilding the same source in each environment, compare the resulting image digests before promotion.

Infrastructure, RBAC, topology or ingestion-selection changes require the full workflow, not deploy-only. Changing a selection does not delete previously deployed resources or revoke old permissions; retirement is separately authorized.

docs.title: Change a runtime setting
docs.text:
First check Deployment settings for ownership and overwrite behavior. Provisioning-managed inputs must be changed in their source and applied through the full workflow. For a directly managed, nonsecret runtime key:

az appconfig kv set --endpoint <app-config-endpoint> --auth-mode login \
  --key <KEY> --value <value> --label agent-lz --yes

Restart each affected Container App revision to reload configuration:

az containerapp revision restart -g <resource-group> -n <container-app-name> \
  --revision <revision-name>

For a hosted version, run root azd deploy with the compatible handoff. Process environment inputs declared in hosted-agent/azure.yaml are immutable version inputs and require a new agent version. An App Configuration edit cannot replace a process-only setting such as APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY. Use agent-lz within each environment's separate configuration store.

docs.title: Rotate a secret
docs.text: Inspect the Key Vault reference before rotating. An unversioned URI resolves the current secret version when configuration reloads; a versioned URI must be updated deliberately. Add the new secret version through your approved secure process, preserve required access, then restart affected Container App revisions or redeploy the hosted version. Verify the new credential before retiring the old one. Never place secrets in plaintext App Configuration or command logs.

docs.title: Recover hosted runtime access
docs.text:
The Agent Application post-deploy hook normally bootstraps the discovered runtime principal. To review the exact read-only role plan from the root's selected environment:

python -m config.deployment.hosted_access --azd-env --plan

An authorized administrator can reconcile only that plan with the idempotent wrapper:

pwsh scripts/bootstrapHostedAccess.ps1

On Linux/macOS use ./scripts/bootstrapHostedAccess.sh. The wrapper selects hosted-agent / orchestrator-agent by default; custom services use their own project/service context. Allow role propagation, then retry root azd deploy so the greeting and remaining deployment gates run before cutover.

The closed bootstrap set grants App Configuration Data Reader, model access and, when configured, access to the exact audit secret. It is not a grant to delegated users or a replacement for all capability profiles. Do not grant Owner or remove unrelated assignments to recover. See hosted identities.

docs.title: Remove an environment
docs.text:
Destructive action

Use the commands below only for an environment whose entire deletion scope is dedicated to this deployment and approved for removal. Confirm the subscription, resource group and deletion prompt. Export or back up required documents, indexes, configuration and conversation data. If the scope contains shared resources or retained data, stop and arrange itemized removal with the owners instead. Check retention obligations first.

For the multi-group path, inventory every configured destination and its shared dependencies before cleanup. The root group alone is not the complete inventory. A predown safety hook blocks azd down for split-group deployments, with no automatic deletion or bypass option.

Arrange itemized, owner-approved manual removal instead; do not bypass the hook or delete shared groups. Additional groups created by the feature are not tagged azd-env-name. Partial provisioning is not authorization to delete a group. The single-group path below is unchanged.

azd env select <environment-name>
azd env get-value AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
azd down

Do not add purge options as a retry. Permanent deletion requires separate authorization and removes recovery options. Reused resources outside the deletion scope and manually created links can remain and continue incurring charges. For a spoke, retire only its own hub peering/DNS links with their owners; do not delete shared hub, DNS or monitoring resources.

docs.title: Related runbooks
docs.text:
• Connect Copilot Studio to a private Foundry agent
  • Deploy infra only
  • Deploy with Azure DevOps for optional reviewed promotion and automation

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Confirm the intended application revisions are running, not placeholders:

    git rev-parse HEAD
git -C ../agent-app-orchestrator rev-parse HEAD
git -C ../agent-app-ui rev-parse HEAD
azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
azd env get-value AZURE_APP_RESOURCE_GROUP
az containerapp list -g <application-resource-group> \
  --query "[].{name:name,state:properties.runningStatus,revision:properties.latestReadyRevisionName}" -o table

    Compare the platform commit with your approved record and each component commit with its manifest.json entry. Inspect source worktrees for unexpected edits; matching HEAD alone does not prove the built source was unchanged.

  2. Read AZURE_CONTAINER_REGISTRY_ENDPOINT for the registry login hostname. The hosted repository is HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE when explicitly set, otherwise agent-app-orchestrator, as declared in hosted-agent/azure.yaml. Use that registry's resource name, repository and recorded digest below:

    azd env get-value HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION
az acr repository show --name <registry-name> \
  --image <hosted-repository>@<sha256-digest> --query digest -o tsv

    Expect the exact same sha256: value, not merely matching tags. In Foundry, inspect the routed version's image and confirm it uses that digest.

  3. Open the frontend URL from the deployment outputs or UI ingress configuration. Use a connected browser for private endpoints. Complete Entra sign-in and delegated authentication.

  4. Exercise an agent task and configured tools with representative identities. For documents, ingest a harmless test document through the configured source. After resolving the protected-retrieval integration gate, test both permitted retrieval and denial to a user without that document's permission. Test uploads only when their additional capabilities are selected.
  5. Correlate the task with runtime telemetry. The deployment's greeting checks basic response only; test actual UI login, OBO and source authorization.

Record unmet capability gates as blocked, not passed. Without validated continuity, chat context lasts only for the active UI session. Default deployment does not promise persistent history, feedback integration or uploads. Use Troubleshooting for failures.

For optional channel distribution after acceptance, use the Publish to Teams and M365 runbook. Publication is not part of this deployment.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
1. Stop promotion and record the failed revision, inputs and deployed state. Select the previous tested complete compatible combination, not an independent component tip. Check compatibility with current data and settings.
  2. Restore the recorded platform commit, manifest, definition and reviewed parameters without overwriting uncommitted work. Align existing sibling checkouts with the restored manifest after preserving their local work.
  3. Preview infrastructure or configuration reversals before applying them. Keep the approved authentication and network posture.
  4. Follow Step 4 with the previous compatible source and inputs: provision, then deploy; deployment prepares the pinned image automatically. If retaining an operator-managed digest, verify its availability and compatibility; deployment does not rebuild it. If restoring older tooling, follow that tooling's own required deployment sequence.
  5. Restore directly managed runtime keys separately from the source checkout, reload affected components and repeat Validation before cutover.

Restoring code does not restore data or reverse schema changes. If reversal is unsupported, arrange an approved forward repair or service-specific recovery. Do not delete the environment as rollback.

docs.title: Objective
docs.text: Provision the Azure foundation without building or deploying application images. Use the Agent Landing Zone repository and its incorporated infra/ source, including when no Agent Application images will be deployed.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text: Use this runbook when you need foundation resources first, or will supply your own application. To deploy the Agent Application now, use the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Complete the permissions and tooling prerequisites. The deployment requires Git, Azure CLI, azd, PowerShell 7, Python and the platform hook dependencies. Review the resource inventory and cost scenarios and regional capacity caveats. Infrastructure-only still creates billable resources.

Blocks marked bash use Bash syntax. In PowerShell, put commands with a trailing backslash (\) on one line and remove the continuation backslashes. Replace every <placeholder> before running a command.

The effective footprint is the combination of enabled services, resource-reuse inputs, application definition, orchestrator topology and network settings. This determines which AI services, backing resources, runtimes, data stores, monitoring, networking and optional add-ons are deployed. Review the root main.parameters.json, Bicep conditions and preview to identify the resources for your deployment.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone Agent Landing Zone
docs.text:
Use this source for infrastructure-only and full-stack deployments:

git clone https://github.com/Azure/agent-landing-zone.git
cd agent-landing-zone

Run all lifecycle commands from this root, not from infra/. Its infra/ is repository-owned source. manifest.json records the coordinated component pins; infra.source records historical incorporation provenance, not a second repository to clone or a separate foundation version to deploy.

Set up Python from the cloned repository before lifecycle commands.

docs.title: Step 2: Create and confirm the target
docs.text:
Replace the placeholders for a new, dedicated environment:

az login
azd auth login
az account set --subscription <subscription-id>
azd env new <environment-name>
azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <subscription-id>
azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP <dedicated-resource-group>
azd env set AZURE_LOCATION <region>

Use azd env select <environment-name> for an existing environment and keep its approved inputs.

Use separate environment, resource-group, identity, configuration and data boundaries for each stage; protect local .azure/ state. Fork or mirror the source only when maintaining your own inputs or automation.

The Bicep deployment through azd uses three resource groups by default:

Group What it contains Default name Foundry Foundry and its related resources The AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP name you set above Application The selected application's services and data resources The same name with -app added Network Workload networking and private connectivity resources The same name with -network added

For example, choosing rg-agent-dev above gives you rg-agent-dev, rg-agent-dev-app and rg-agent-dev-network.

The deployment scripts, also called hooks, create missing application and network groups. The identity running deployment needs permission to create them. If an administrator creates those groups in advance, set CREATE_RESOURCE_GROUPS=false so the scripts do not create groups.

To use different group names or combine resources into one or two groups, set the resource group destinations before first provision.

Run one azd provision command from the repository root to deploy across all three groups. Do not run a separate deployment for each group. These instructions apply to Bicep with azd; Terraform and portal deployments have their own settings.

docs.title: Step 3: Choose the network setup
docs.text:
For production and workloads with sensitive data, use private service endpoints. Choose a self-contained private network or connect the workload's private network to an existing corporate hub. Both options are described below.

The template currently defaults to NETWORK_ISOLATION=false. Set it to true explicitly for a private deployment; the template default is not the recommended production configuration.

Use azd env set for the individual settings shown below. For example, azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true selects private networking for the selected environment.

Settings containing a list of values or a group of related fields, such as allowed IP ranges or the network address plan, go in the root main.parameters.json file. See Existing networks, private DNS and parameter files below for details.

DEPLOYMENT_MODE identifies the network design, but does not configure routing, DNS or isolation by itself. Configure those through the settings for your chosen approach below. DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY separately chooses where the orchestrator runs. See How it works for how deployment settings are applied.

docs.title: Private standalone network
docs.text:
Choose this when your workload team will manage its own network, private DNS and outbound firewall rather than use shared hub services.

azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true
azd env set DEPLOYMENT_MODE standalone
azd env set DEPLOY_AZURE_FIREWALL true
azd env set DEPLOY_JUMPBOX true
azd env set DEPLOY_BASTION true
azd env set DEPLOY_NAT_GATEWAY true

Review the standalone reference for nonoverlapping subnets, network security groups (NSGs), outbound routing and private DNS. For native Bastion Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP), choose BASTION_SKU_NAME=Standard and BASTION_ENABLE_TUNNELING=true; portal access does not require the native tunneling workflow. Have a connected host ready for Agent post-provision configuration, or use explicit deferral below.

docs.title: Private spoke using an existing hub
docs.text:
Choose this when your organization already provides shared networking services. The workload gets its own private network, called a spoke, connected to that shared hub.

Agree hub routing, reverse peering, DNS and permissions with their owners first. For a new spoke VNet with a hub firewall:

azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION true
azd env set DEPLOYMENT_MODE ailz-integrated
azd env set DEPLOY_AZURE_FIREWALL false
azd env set DEPLOY_BASTION false
azd env set DEPLOY_NAT_GATEWAY false
azd env set DEPLOY_JUMPBOX true
azd env set EXISTING_BASTION_RESOURCE_ID <hub-bastion-resource-id>
azd env set HUB_INTEGRATION_HUB_VNET_RESOURCE_ID <hub-vnet-resource-id>
azd env set HUB_INTEGRATION_CREATE_HUB_PEERING true
azd env set HUB_INTEGRATION_EGRESS_NEXT_HOP_IP <hub-firewall-private-ip>

Instead of a next-hop IP, a platform-managed route table can be selected with HUB_INTEGRATION_EXISTING_ROUTE_TABLE_RESOURCE_ID; these inputs are mutually exclusive. Set one when hub egress is required. Shared monitoring uses EXISTING_LOG_ANALYTICS_WORKSPACE_RESOURCE_ID and, when applicable, EXISTING_APPLICATION_INSIGHTS_RESOURCE_ID with its protected connection string.

Apply the hub-and-spoke DNS and peering contract before provisioning. A network operator may need to complete reverse peering and DNS links as soon as a fresh spoke VNet exists, before bootstrap can finish. Use an approved production hub, not the infra/tests/hub/ fixture.

docs.title: Public service endpoints
docs.text:
Use this option only for an organization-approved, short-lived evaluation or demonstration with synthetic or non-sensitive data, when private connectivity is not available. It is not the recommended production setup.

The commands below select public service endpoints, not private networking. Authentication and authorization are still required, but they do not prevent network access to those public endpoints or make them private.

Use a separate test environment. Do not disable isolation on an existing private environment to fix a deployment or connectivity failure.

azd env set NETWORK_ISOLATION false
azd env set DEPLOYMENT_MODE standalone

docs.title: Existing networks, private DNS and parameter files
docs.text:
Choice Required review Existing VNet Choose subnet ownership and apply the matching inputs. Both peering directions are externally managed for BYO VNet Shared private DNS Supply the applicable EXISTING_PRIVATE_DNS_ZONE_*_RESOURCE_ID inputs. Their owner supplies VNet links or resolver forwarding; peering alone does not propagate DNS Azure Policy-managed DNS Use POLICY_MANAGED_PRIVATE_DNS=true instead of BYO zone overrides and agree who creates zone groups, records and links Approved public exception Review native allowedIpRanges and Storage trusted-service/resource-instance exceptions to confirm the approved service-specific public access Controlled public frontend Review Application Gateway ingress, certificate ownership, WAF policy and cost before opting in

Use azd env set for settings documented as environment variables that take one value, such as NETWORK_ISOLATION. Put settings containing lists or groups of related fields, such as the complete address plan, allowedIpRanges, Storage controls and publicIngress, in the reviewed root main.parameters.json.

Platform hooks regenerate infra/main.parameters.json; do not edit that generated copy. The parameter reference describes foundation inputs; Deployment settings describes platform composition and overrides.

docs.title: Bind the future application
docs.text:
Choose the orchestrator topology and ingestion selection now, even if images will be deployed later. For a different application:

azd env set AGENTLZ_APP_DEFINITION <path-to-app-definition.json>

Otherwise use the Agent Application definition. The first provision binds the environment to its application ID; a different ID requires a new environment. Preserve the existing layout and ingestion selection during recovery.

The default Agent layout is hosted-no-panel, using maf_lite and Foundry IQ without Agent App Ingestion. Set HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE to the approved delegated Foundry audience followed by /.default before provisioning, even when application deployment will happen later. See the linked full-stack runbook for the identity inputs and protected-retrieval integration gate.

docs.title: Step 4: Preview and provision
docs.text:
Review the selected application's runtime egress plan before approving provisioning: python -m config.deployment.egress --plan --environment <environment-name>. This command is local and read-only; it does not run the preparation hook or create resource groups.

First run azd hooks run preup to validate the definition and binding before azd's resource-group initialization. Normal azd provision automatically runs the Agent preprovision hook to compose parameters and bootstrap authorized additional groups. Manual preparation is needed only if you choose to preview first.

docs.title: Optional preview
docs.text:
Preview preparation can create resource groups

With azd 1.37.1, azd provision --preview does not run preprovision hooks. It reads the existing infra/main.parameters.json, which may still be the checked-in seed or another environment's composition, and cannot bootstrap missing additional destination groups.

Before an optional preview, select the intended azd environment, activate the prepared Python environment and run one matching hook from the platform root: pwsh -File scripts/preProvision.ps1 on Windows, or sh scripts/preProvision.sh on Linux/macOS. These hooks load selected azd values, compose parameters and can create missing additional groups when CREATE_RESOURCE_GROUPS=true. Otherwise those groups must already exist, or a composed split-group preview can fail with NotFound.

Native preview can also create the empty Foundry/root resource group. Neither fresh-environment preparation nor preview is guaranteed write-free; authorize group creation before running them. A successful preview does not prove private connectivity, service configuration or application readiness.

After this preparation, the optional preview command is:

azd provision --preview

If previewing, review its scopes, names, routes, resource changes, public access and role assignments. Resolve quota, Policy, subnet and capacity findings rather than skipping preflight.

docs.title: Provision
docs.text:
With the resource changes approved, provision normally:

azd provision

Test connectivity after provisioning and application behavior after deploying your selected application.

Provisioning completes validation and binding, foundation deployment, then service configuration, role reconciliation and App Configuration publication unless explicitly deferred. It does not build or deploy application images.

Selected Container Apps can run placeholder images at this point. A placeholder response checks basic network and runtime reachability. Validate sign-in, tools, ingestion and document authorization after deploying the Agent Application. For initial infrastructure provisioning, inspect platform outputs below and continue to Validation. Use lifecycle tasks only when needed.

docs.title: Platform outputs
docs.text:
After configuration completes, App Configuration publishes the JSON AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS and matching flat keys under label agent-lz. Search and Cosmos sections are omitted when their endpoints are absent; other required fields must validate. These derived keys are not written back to the azd environment.

Flat key JSON path AGENTLZ_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT foundry.projectEndpoint AGENTLZ_FOUNDRY_ACCOUNT_NAME foundry.accountName AGENTLZ_ACR_LOGIN_SERVER registry.loginServer AGENTLZ_APPCONFIG_ENDPOINT appConfig.endpoint AGENTLZ_SEARCH_ENDPOINT search.endpoint AGENTLZ_STORAGE_BLOB_ENDPOINT storage.blobEndpoint AGENTLZ_COSMOS_ENDPOINT cosmos.endpoint AGENTLZ_KEYVAULT_URI keyVault.uri

AGENTLZ_NETWORK_ISOLATED records isolation. AGENTLZ_IDENTITY_<COMPONENT>_CLIENT_ID and the JSON identities array contain discovered Container App identity client IDs, not principal IDs. Hosted runtime identities are created later, during application deployment. Missing or ambiguous identities fail publication; system-assigned identity resolution also requires the exact Entra service-principal read. AGENTLZ_COMPONENT_IDENTITIES is an explicit override input, not an automatic output.

az appconfig kv show --endpoint <app-configuration-endpoint> \
  --key AGENTLZ_PLATFORM_OUTPUTS --label agent-lz --auth-mode login

If only output publication needs refreshing after successful configuration:

azd env refresh
python -m config.deployment.outputs

This does not replace deferred or failed service configuration.

docs.title: Complete a deferred post-provision
docs.text:
Private configuration can be explicitly deferred by RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX=false, or by AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING=true when RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX is not truthy. Set the approved deferral before the first provision when the connected host does not exist yet. Successful provisioning then reports that application setup is incomplete. Deferral does not bypass earlier topology/private-service checks.

On a new connected host, restore the same reviewed source revision and root parameter file. Install the prerequisites and Python dependencies, authenticate both CLIs, then initialize local state only if absent:

azd env new <same-environment-name>
azd env set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID <subscription-id>
azd env set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP <existing-resource-group>
azd env set AZURE_LOCATION <region>
azd env refresh

If the environment is already present, select it instead. Reapply the approved deployment inputs: refresh restores outputs, not your full configuration.

For the multi-group path, restore the same approved application/network destination mapping as well; the root group alone is not sufficient. Securely restore .azure/<same-environment-name>/resource-groups.json from that environment's original host before running its hooks. Output refresh does not recreate this immutable destination binding; do not generate or edit a replacement to bypass the check.

Do not publish or copy another stage's .azure/ state as an input artifact. An authorized runner can use managed-identity sign-in. Verify its scoped configuration and build roles before running the hooks.

From the connected host, clear deferral and finish configuration:

azd env set RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX true
azd env set AZURE_SKIP_NETWORK_ISOLATION_WARNING false
azd hooks run postprovision

RUN_FROM_JUMPBOX requests connectivity checks on the connected host. Verify platform outputs and required data-plane access before deploying. Private native Blob sources can require an administrator to approve the exact Search shared private-link request reported by the readiness gate. Do not approve every pending connection or bypass the gate.

docs.title: Reconfigure the foundation
docs.text:
Record the deployed source revision, approved parameters, outputs and dependent applications. Back up required data and configuration, check compatibility and retain existing names, locations, layout and ingestion intent. If previewing changes, repeat the selected-environment preparation before reviewing the preview. Apply approved root parameter changes with the provisioning step above.

Integrate the coordinated platform and its infra/ tree together; do not replace only its foundation folder from another repository. Use the reapply procedure and rollback in the Deploy full stack runbook.

Retry a partial deployment with the same approved revision and environment after repairing the specific failure. Review resource and data changes separately when reverting code. Do not delete data, rename subnets, move existing resources to another region, weaken isolation or bypass preflight to recover. Turning a deploy flag off is not deletion or permission cleanup.

docs.title: Add an application later
docs.text: Deploy the same bound application and selected components. Follow Step 4 of the Deploy full stack runbook: run azd deploy from the configured foundation. Deployment automatically prepares the hosted image and its handoff; no second provision is required. Custom definitions follow their own component contract.

docs.title: Remove the foundation
docs.text: Use the safe environment removal procedure from the selected source root and environment. Confirm ownership and backups before deletion. For a spoke, have network/DNS owners remove only the recorded spoke-specific attachments and preserve shared services. Purge is a separate irreversible decision, not a normal retry or rollback.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
1. Inspect the selected target and inventory:

    azd env get-value AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
azd env get-value AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP
az resource list -g <resource-group> --query "[].{name:name,type:type}" -o table
az network private-endpoint list -g <resource-group> \
  --query "[].{name:name,state:provisioningState,connections:privateLinkServiceConnections[].privateLinkServiceConnectionState.status}" -o json

    For the multi-group path, repeat resource inventory for every distinct destination, and inspect private endpoints in their actual group. Do not infer a Foundry or network resource's group from the application group.

  2. Compare the inventory with enabled features and reuse inputs. Account for both new and reused resources.

  3. For private deployments, verify approved connections, private DNS and TCP/TLS reachability from the actual deployment host. Use the standalone checks or hub checks.
  4. Test required service operations with the authorized configuration identity and confirm telemetry reaches the intended workspace.
  5. Inspect post-provision logs and platform outputs. Record explicit deferral or any logged configuration failure as incomplete. A placeholder HTTP response does not prove application readiness.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
1. Stop retries and record which resources and configuration changed. If only local inputs changed, restore reviewed inputs before provisioning.
  2. Compare previous inputs with deployed state. Preview the previous compatible source and parameters with azd provision --preview from the selected root, following the Agent preview preparation when applicable.
  3. Apply with azd provision only if reviewed changes preserve data, shared resources and the approved network posture.
  4. Repeat Validation. If inputs cannot safely reverse a change, stop and arrange service-specific forward repair or recovery with its owner.

Successful provisioning does not restore deleted data or reverse schema changes. Disabling a flag does not delete resources or revoke grants. Use the separately authorized removal procedure only for intentional retirement, not as a retry.

docs.title: Embed chat
docs.text:
Agent App UI provides a floating Chainlit Copilot widget for an existing portal. Its script renders in an open Shadow DOM, a separate part of the portal page's document structure, not an iframe containing another web page.

This is Agent App UI embedding, not Copilot Studio. The UI remains in Container Apps, with the orchestrator hosted in Foundry and grounding through Foundry IQ. The pinned UI embedding reference contains the component integration contract.

This page describes requirements, not a turnkey portal integration. Portal token acquisition, Content Security Policy (CSP) and widget lifecycle require application work. Infrastructure deployment and component reloads follow the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: UI and portal contract
docs.text:
The portal has its own Entra client registration and acquires a delegated v2 access token for the UI API. The API exposes user_impersonation; an ID token or Graph token is not valid. The portal's delegated API permissions and consent are separate from the UI's server-side Foundry OBO exchange. Agent Application access explains that downstream path.

UI runtime setting Entra embedding contract CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENABLED true enables embedding; default is disabled. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_AUTH_MODE entra. CHAINLIT_URL Canonical UI HTTPS origin, for example https://chat.contoso.com. CHAINLIT_ALLOWED_ORIGINS Exact distinct portal HTTPS origins, for example https://portal.contoso.com. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENTRA_TENANT_ID Issuing Entra tenant's unique ID. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENTRA_AUDIENCE Expected UI API access-token aud. CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENTRA_REQUIRED_SCOPE Scope name, normally user_impersonation.

Origins contain only scheme, host and optional port, without wildcard, null, credentials, path, query or fragment. CHAINLIT_ROOT_PATH must be empty. The validator accepts the configured tenant and v2 issuer only. For v2 tokens, aud is normally the API's application client ID, while the requested scope uses the API's fully qualified URI. Access token claims describes the distinction.

These are UI runtime settings, normally under App Configuration label agent-lz, not azd deployment inputs. Nonempty process environment values override embedding settings. The UI loads them at startup. Deployment settings identifies their configuration boundary. The existing session-signing secret stays protected.

The widget requires one Uvicorn process, one active Container Apps revision and exactly one replica because sessions and rate limits are process-local. Same-site HTTPS subdomains work with the default CHAINLIT_COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax. Cross-site portals require none, with Secure and HttpOnly cookies, but browser third-party-cookie policy can still prevent a session. A standalone UI link remains available if browser cookie policy blocks embedding.

docs.title: Browser and gateway boundaries
docs.text:
The portal CSP must permit scripts from the controlled UI origin and HTTPS and secure WebSocket (WSS) connections to it. The bundle runs with the portal page's JavaScript privileges; Shadow DOM does not isolate security.

It also injects inline styles, which can conflict with the portal's CSP. A compatible policy retains the portal's nonce/hash protections rather than broadly enabling unsafe-inline. Embedding does not require weakening frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options.

The gateway contract preserves the external UI origin, cookies, browser Origin, and WebSocket upgrades. Required paths include /copilot/index.js, /copilot/auth/bootstrap, /copilot/auth/logout, /project/settings, /ws/socket.io polling/upgrades and /api/download/{grant_token}. Container Apps ingress supports WebSockets. Browsers still need authorized network access to private UI ingress; embedding does not make it public.

The origin allow-list constrains browsers, not arbitrary HTTP clients that can forge Origin. Entra validation and network/gateway authorization remain necessary.

docs.title: Session lifecycle
docs.text:
The portal's Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) integration acquires the UI API token in memory. A credentialed POST /copilot/auth/bootstrap carries it in the bearer header before the widget mounts. Bootstrap validates token and user admission, then creates an opaque server-side session cookie. The token is not a widget accessToken and does not belong in a URL, local storage or portal source.

The embedded session retains the delegated token server-side for the hosted client's OBO exchange. HOSTED_AGENT_AUTH_MODE=user_delegated preserves that caller boundary. Protected document access still requires the hosted retrieval integration; embedding does not supply it.

Session lifetime ends at the earlier of token expiry and CHAINLIT_COPILOT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS (default 3600 seconds). It has no silent standalone OAuth refresh. Logout/account switching requires widget unmount, local thread-state cleanup and credentialed POST /copilot/auth/logout before another account's bootstrap. Restart, revision switch and eviction invalidate the process-local session and download-grant state.

docs.title: Integration evidence
docs.text:
Successful bootstrap and cookie acceptance allow /project/settings and the chat socket to authenticate. Invalid/expired tokens return 401; disallowed origins return 403. Expiry can also surface as WebSocket 4401 or Socket.IO authentication failure. Bootstrap throttling returns 429 with Retry-After; authoritative rate limits need gateway enforcement.

An integration is incomplete without account-switch, logout, cookie-policy and two-user document allow/deny tests. Do not work around token failures with anonymous fallback or service-identity retrieval.

docs.title: Disabling embedding
docs.text: The portal widget and CHAINLIT_COPILOT_ENABLED control different sides of the integration. Disabling the UI setting takes effect after a UI process reload. It does not remove standalone chat or alter the hosted agent.

docs.title: Unsupported edges
docs.text:
• Iframes, same-origin subpaths and multi-process/multi-replica embedded sessions are unsupported by this widget integration.
  • Anonymous embedding supplies no user token and cannot call the default user-delegated hosted path. It disables durable threads, uploads and private citation downloads; its endpoint is independent of portal login.
  • Upload controls require the separately deployed ingestion capability. Embedding does not add native hosted-agent uploads.

A separately authenticated client is an application extension under Bring your own app.

docs.title: Fabric IQ
docs.text:
Fabric grounding queries data where it lives rather than ingesting a copy into a landing-zone index. A Fabric data agent answers analytical questions over its configured data, including Power BI semantic models. A Fabric IQ ontology binds business entities and relationships to data.

This page explains the native knowledge-source options and integration gaps. Deployment procedures are in the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Data agents and ontologies are different sources
docs.text:
Foundry IQ source Fabric object fabricDataAgent A published data agent, identified by workspace ID and data agent item ID. fabricOntology An ontology, identified by workspace ID and ontology item ID.

A semantic model ID is neither a data agent ID nor an ontology ID. These remote sources query Fabric at retrieval time and do not need Agent App Ingestion. Both knowledge-source integrations are preview. Microsoft documents data agent sources and ontology sources separately.

docs.title: Fabric access and governance
docs.text:
A data agent needs a supported capacity, tenant settings, configured data sources and publication. Consumers need access to both the agent and its underlying data. For the semantic-model data-agent path, Microsoft specifies Read permission on the model; Build permission is not required for that interaction. Authoring permissions are separate. The Fabric data agent guide describes the Fabric-side procedure.

Search and the Fabric workspace must share an Entra tenant. Data permissions, model row-level security and regional data-handling requirements still apply. Private Azure networking does not configure Fabric workspace networking. Preview and cross-service data movement require governance review.

docs.title: What the accelerator registers
docs.text:
FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_ENABLED, FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME, FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_WORKSPACE_ID and FABRIC_DATA_AGENT_DATA_AGENT_ID describe data-agent source registration. The separate ontology inputs are FABRIC_IQ_ENABLED, FABRIC_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME, FABRIC_IQ_WORKSPACE_ID and FABRIC_IQ_ONTOLOGY_ID.

The Deployment settings register sources and knowledge-base references in Search. They do not create Fabric items, grant model access or deliver user tokens. Runtime selects sources by enabled flag and name. Provisioning can overwrite manual edits to platform-owned objects.

docs.title: Integration work still required
docs.text:
Hosted Agent Application does not have a configuration-only Fabric path. For a native data-agent source, the following boundaries need coordinated work:

Boundary Product contract and accelerator gap Delegated identity Fabric uses a Search-audience user token in x-ms-query-source-authorization, separately from Search service authentication. The hosted entrypoint supplies empty user context and cannot forward that token through the retrieval strategy. Retrieval reasoning Fabric data-agent sources require low or medium. The accelerator's native-source knowledge-base template emits minimal and no planning model. There is no native-branch environment override that fixes this. Response parsing The documented data-agent response uses sourceData.fabricAnswer and fabricEmbeddedResources. The connector's data-agent parser expects dataAgentAnswer and dataAgentRawData. Its ontology fallback can read fabricAnswer, but misclassifies the source and does not handle the embedded resources. API compatibility Source setup and the connector default to 2026-05-01-preview. Current Microsoft examples use 2026-08-01-preview; registration, retrieve requests and response parsing need validation together.

The official data-agent source contract defines the token audience and response fields. Source registration alone cannot resolve these gaps. A reviewed template change needs supported reasoning and model configuration, and a reviewed application integration needs trusted user delegation and compatible parsing.

An ontology remains a separate source contract, not a substitute data-agent identifier or parser. It also requires low or medium reasoning and validated user delegation through the hosted boundary. Foundry IQ explains how knowledge bases relate to Foundry Agent Service tools; the custom application runbook covers delivery of reviewed application changes.

Tokens remain server-side, outside prompts and user-supplied tool arguments. Authorization comes from validated caller context, not model-provided user IDs or group lists.

docs.title: Acceptance and recovery
docs.text:
A known-answer query must first succeed in the published Fabric agent as the intended consumer. End-to-end acceptance then includes the correct source reference, expected analytical result and any returned structured resources. It also includes a user denied model access, users with different row-level security and a missing-token test.

Broader managed-identity grants cannot repair missing delegation. Recovery restores the previous application and settings, removes only the pilot source reference and retains Fabric items or Search objects still used elsewhere. Approved application changes start a new hosted version through the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Foundry IQ
docs.text:
A knowledge source describes searchable content. A knowledge base binds one or more sources and controls retrieval. Foundry Agent Service can call that knowledge base as a native tool, so the agent can ground answers in retrieved content and return source references.

This page describes Foundry IQ and the Agent Application's integration limits. Deployment follows the Deploy full stack runbook.

docs.title: Managed and remote sources
docs.text:
Indexed sources copy content into Search for retrieval. Remote sources query their service at request time, without copying the source corpus into a local index. Both can return content to the agent and model.

The accelerator defaults to a native Blob source, container documents, standard content extraction and ingestion permission options ["rbacScope"]. Search manages the generated indexing assets. Optional Agent App Ingestion is disabled by default for new environments and is not needed for this source. Ingestion explains native source ingestion, conversation uploads and custom processing.

An existing Search index can be registered as a searchIndex knowledge source. The pipeline that owns that index remains responsible for its content, schema and permission metadata. Registering it does not populate or authorize it. Microsoft documents Blob sources and Search index sources separately.

SharePoint, Work IQ and Fabric IQ describe additional native sources, including previews, and the work needed to integrate them with Agent Application.

docs.title: Native tools and the accelerator boundary
docs.text:
Microsoft's Foundry Agent Service connection guide connects a knowledge base through its MCP endpoint and a Foundry RemoteTool project connection. The connection belongs to the agent's native tool definition.

The accelerator also provisions a Microsoft Entra ID-authenticated CognitiveSearch project connection and publishes KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONNECTION_ID. The shipped retrieval connector does not consume that ID. It calls the Search endpoint and knowledge base name directly. A provisioned connection alone does not attach a native tool or establish user delegation in the hosted application. A CognitiveSearch connection is not the RemoteTool connection in the native-tool procedure.

The relevant Deployment settings describe distinct objects. The connector reads runtime values from App Configuration with label agent-lz.

Setting Meaning in the shipped connector RETRIEVAL_BACKEND foundry_iq selects knowledge-base retrieval in this connector; it does not attach a native agent tool. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_ENDPOINT Search service root, such as https://<service>.search.windows.net, not a Foundry project or retrieve URL. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_NAME Knowledge-base object name, not an index name. FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_NAME Primary registered source name. FOUNDRY_IQ_PATTERN and FOUNDRY_IQ_KNOWLEDGE_SOURCE_KIND azureBlob for the default source, or matching searchIndex for an existing index. FOUNDRY_IQ_API_VERSION The source and connector contract defaults to 2026-05-01-preview. KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONNECTION_ID Provisioned project connection metadata, not a connector target selector.

Current Microsoft source examples use contracts beyond the accelerator's default API. Adopting a source requires compatibility across registration, retrieve requests and response parsing, not an API-version edit alone.

Hosted user authorization is not wired end to end

The shipped hosted entrypoint supplies empty user context to the retrieval strategy. It does not forward the delegated user token required by the connector's OBO path. Authenticated retrieval fails closed without that token. Native service support and UI sign-in do not resolve this boundary. Protected retrieval requires a reviewed integration that carries validated per-user context from invocation to the selected retrieval tool.

That integration must retain Foundry's trusted call context, service authentication and each source's permission enforcement. Tokens do not belong in prompts, chat history or user-supplied tool arguments. Application authentication and the custom application runbook cover the surrounding application work.

docs.title: Ownership and connectivity
docs.text:
Platform Search setup reconciles named sources and knowledge bases from config/search/search.j2. Later provisioning can replace manual additions to those objects. Operator-owned sources and knowledge bases need distinct names; changes to platform-owned objects belong in reviewed templates. Knowledge-base updates must preserve all intended source references.

Source administration, ingestion and retrieval use separate permissions: the administrator manages knowledge objects; Search's ingestion identity reads the source and calls extraction/embedding services; the retrieval identity authenticates to Search; the end user's delegated identity authorizes protected content. A service role is not a substitute for user authorization.

Private deployments need both runtime-to-Search access and Search-to-source/model connectivity. The platform attempts to set generated Blob indexers to private execution, but skips that update if an indexer does not yet exist. Generated indexer state and shared private-link approvals still need validation before sensitive ingestion. See Network isolation.

docs.title: Acceptance and recovery
docs.text:
Acceptance includes successful source indexing where applicable, a known-answer query with the expected document reference, and separate allowed/denied-user tests. A denied result must exclude the restricted document and its citation. A missing-token failure calls for identity integration work, not anonymous retrieval or broader managed-identity grants.

Configuration is cached in the running application. Approved changes require the Deploy full stack runbook to start a new hosted version. Recovery restores the previous compatible image and settings while retaining source documents and knowledge objects.

docs.title: Hosted agents
docs.text: Agent App Orchestrator runs as a container in Foundry Agent Service. The fresh default is DEPLOYMENT_TOPOLOGY=hosted-no-panel with maf_lite orchestration. The UI remains in Azure Container Apps. This page explains the hosting contract; the Deploy full stack runbook contains the ordered deployment and recovery procedures.

docs.title: Topologies
docs.text:
Hosted topology Orchestrator Administrative panel Agent Application Cosmos DB hosted-no-panel (default) Foundry hosted container Not deployed Not deployed

The table describes default application resources, not Foundry Agent Service's own backing resources. This layout does not activate history, feedback or operator access. Those capabilities have independent integration and validation gates. Agent App Ingestion is selected separately, as described in Ingestion and conversation uploads.

docs.title: Image and deployment handoff
docs.text: Hosted deployment separates foundation provisioning from application deployment. azd provision creates the project, registry, network and access prerequisites, not a running agent or a placeholder. azd deploy automatically builds the manifest-pinned orchestrator with the supported hosted startup command when needed, records an immutable digest, binds the image to the provisioned foundation and creates the agent version. No separate preparation command or second provision is needed; azd up performs the full workflow. Private builds still use the VNet's ACR Tasks agent pool.

docs.title: Redeploy the same image or prepare a new one
docs.text:
Change Deployment contract Same generated digest, matching source and startup provenance Deployment reuses the image. Missing image or changed generated source/startup provenance Deployment builds the manifest-pinned image and updates the handoff without reprovisioning. Changed hosted process environment or cached runtime settings A new agent version is required, potentially with the same compatible digest. Explicit digest without generated-source provenance Compatibility and registry availability are operator-owned. Deployment does not replace it automatically.

Generated images are reused only when the recorded source revision and startup command match. To supply an independently built image, set HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION to its canonical digest and clear HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_COMMIT and HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_STARTUP_COMMAND_SHA256. The image must be available in the selected registry and repository and already use the hosted entrypoint. Independent builds of the same source need not produce the same digest. The standalone preparation scripts remain optional compatibility commands; they are not required deployment steps.

The procedure is in application redeployment.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
Deployment settings distinguishes deployment inputs from App Configuration keys and hosted process environment.

Input Contract HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION Immutable sha256: digest with 64 hexadecimal characters; tags are rejected. HOSTED_AGENT_RESOURCE_SCOPE Explicit delegated-user audience ending in /.default; not the UI API scope. HOSTED_AGENT_STARTUP_COMMAND Fixed to uvicorn src.api.hosted_entrypoint:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8088. HOSTED_AGENT_SSE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Stream idle timeout, default 60.

The supplied hosted-agent/azure.yaml declares the agent name, CPU, memory, protocols and startup command as literal fields. Its image and environment fields use azd interpolation. A custom application's source.imageDigest instead becomes AGENTLZ_IMAGE_DIGEST; it is not interchangeable with HOSTED_AGENT_IMAGE_VERSION. See source pinning.

docs.title: Runtime identities and access
docs.text:
Identity Responsibility Deployment principal Provisions resources, creates agent versions and reconciles authorized scoped grants. Foundry project managed identity Pulls the image through the registry grant. Actual deployed agent runtime principal Reads configuration and calls authorized dependencies. Delegated user Needs Foundry project/agent access and permission to requested data.

The post-deploy hook discovers the runtime principal and grants App Configuration Data Reader on the store and Cognitive Services OpenAI User on the Foundry account. If AUDIT_HMAC_KEY is a Key Vault reference, the bootstrap plan also includes Key Vault Secrets User on that individual secret.

Source access, other secrets and caller permissions are outside this closed bootstrap set. Role reconciliation needs scoped role-assignment authority or an authorized administrator applying the reviewed plan. Hosted access recovery contains the operational checks.

Custom services reconcile declared capability profiles against the discovered runtime principal.

docs.title: Delegated UI invocation
docs.text:
Hosted composition routes the UI with CHAT_BACKEND=hosted_agent. The UI defaults to HOSTED_AGENT_AUTH_MODE=user_delegated. It exchanges the signed-in user's UI API token for the Foundry audience through OAuth on-behalf-of (OBO), without fallback to the UI managed identity. Agent Application access explains sign-in and consent. Successful invocation is not evidence of document-level authorization.

The hosted container does not automatically receive the user's bearer token or authenticated principal. Its code controls model calls, retrieval and tools. Portal instructions or tool attachments do not automatically reconfigure maf_lite; Agent tools describes the native Toolbox integration boundary.

docs.title: Protocol and caller access
docs.text:
• Responses 2.0.0 is stateless. Non-null previous_response_id returns HTTP 422. Top-level conversation does not load managed history. Input contains bounded, ordered prior messages ending in the current user message.
  • Agent App UI uses /invocations?api-version=v1. Its conversation_id labels conversation-scoped retrieval; it is not permission to load history. The UI accepts response.conversation.id and response.conversation_id, and rejects malformed or conflicting IDs.
  • A delegated caller needs Foundry project user access and agent access. Deployment permission alone is insufficient.

Publish to Teams and M365 uses Bot Service authorization and the Activity endpoint. Connect Copilot Studio uses an authenticated Power Automate flow and VNet delegation, not the native connected-agent tool. These have different caller-identity contracts from the UI.

docs.title: Continuity, history and the administrative panel
docs.text:
Without continuity, multi-turn context lasts only for the active UI session. Reload, browser restart or a new chat loses that context. The hosted container does not read or write managed Conversations.

HOSTED_CONTINUITY_ENABLED defaults to false. Delegated continuity requires validated owner isolation, Responses protocol at least 2.0.0, and the middle-tier identity's reviewed agent-scoped UserIdentityImpersonation data action. HOSTED_CONVERSATION_OWNER_BINDING_VALIDATED is an evidence gate, not a way to grant those permissions. Provisioning leaves it false. When validated continuity is active, the UI sends the authorized transcript to the stateless container, which still does not load managed history.

Panel user routes additionally require actual panel deployment, PANEL_HISTORY_ENABLED and active continuity; otherwise they return HTTP 503. The panel's delegated enumeration and operator surfaces have separate gates, PANEL_HISTORY_OWNER_BINDING_VALIDATED and PANEL_OPERATOR_SURFACES_ENABLED. They remain false until their own authorization checks have evidence. Cosmos holds owner-index/feedback metadata; managed transcripts reside in Foundry. User feedback explains the missing UI integration.

docs.title: Configuration TLS compatibility
docs.text:
APP_CONFIG_TLS_COMPATIBILITY is an opt-in process environment variable, default false, read before remote configuration. It applies only to the orchestrator loader's configured App Configuration and Key Vault endpoints. The profile uses P-256 and TCP MSS 1200 while retaining certificate/hostname verification, custom CAs, TLS 1.2 or later, credentials and retries. It requires the actual HTTPS KEY_VAULT_URI; invalid input fails startup.

An App Configuration key cannot replace this bootstrap input. A changed value requires a new hosted version. The TLS diagnosis reference covers transport diagnosis without disabling certificate validation.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: Prompt/completion capture is off by default. The deployment input HOSTED_AGENT_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT maps to the hosted process variable OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT. A changed value requires a new agent version. Capture into Application Insights is a data-retention and privacy decision, not a prerequisite for chat.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Agent Landing Zone connects deployment inputs, Azure infrastructure and application code through the Azure Developer CLI (azd). This page introduces those concepts for the Bicep/azd implementation, so you can understand what the deployment does without memorizing commands or parameters.

A command-line interface (CLI) runs commands in a terminal. Bicep describes Azure resources as code; azd coordinates their creation and application deployment. Azure Blob Storage stores files, and Azure AI Search indexes content so the application can retrieve relevant passages. An application programming interface (API) lets code send requests to a service.

An orchestrator coordinates model calls, retrieval and tools. The default Agent Application runs it in Foundry Agent Service with maf_lite, the supplied orchestration strategy (the code path that coordinates a turn). It has no administration panel and uses native Foundry IQ Blob ingestion, where Azure AI Search prepares Blob documents for retrieval.

The sections below explain how that application and its infrastructure are prepared. The Deploy infra only and Deploy full stack runbooks provide the execution steps.

docs.title: How to read deployment settings
docs.text:
A deployment parameter tells the template what to create or reuse, such as a private network or an existing hub. An azd environment groups the settings and deployment state for one deployment, such as development or production. With Bicep and azd, the runbooks use two ways to supply parameter values:

Input form Source Uppercase input, such as NETWORK_ISOLATION The selected azd environment. The platform maps it to a template parameter or reads it in a deployment hook. Native parameter, such as modelDeploymentList The root main.parameters.json, inside parameters.<name>.value, for parameters without an environment-variable mapping.

For example, NETWORK_ISOLATION=true selects private networking. Deployment inputs are resolved before provisioning. The platform combines them with the root parameter file to generate infra/main.parameters.json. The Deployment settings reference lists inputs and defaults; the Deploy infra only and Deploy full stack runbooks provide their application order.

Application-specific runtime settings
